scope: 717 individual Photojournal decisions, all 189 distinct PDS bundles and all 1643 USGS catalogue records retained. Only original screened opportunities and the explicitly expanded leads have proposals. Native scientific qualification remains proposal-specific.

photojournal.title: Global Map of Magnetic Anomalies (MAG/ER)
photojournal.reason: Global radial magnetic map overlays tracks and geological context; original field/altitude data are required under any later Mars proposal.

photojournal.title: MOLA TOPOGRAPHIC MAP
photojournal.reason: MOLA south-polar elevation product has explicit precision and a polar data gap; retain native units and gap if Mars scope later reopens.

photojournal.title: Clouds and Hazes of Jupiter’s Southern Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: Galileo southern true/false-color clouds cover 25°S to the pole; derived color variants belong to one qualified observing set.

photojournal.title: Tempel 1 Composite Map
photojournal.reason: Tempel 1 composite resamples varied-distance images to 5 m pixels; original shape/camera registration is required and uniform pixel scale is not uniform resolution.

photojournal.title: Temperature Map of Tempel 1
photojournal.reason: Tempel 1 infrared thermal fit separates reflected and emitted components; preserve regional support, model assumptions and uncertainty.

photojournal.title: An Infrared Map of Titan
photojournal.reason: Titan 1.6/2.01/5 µm mosaic combines two flybys and measures reflected light; it is not thermal emission or instantaneous global coverage.

photojournal.title: Triton Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Sixteen-frame Triton controlled mosaic belongs to the mission/source family already selected; verify original frame overlap before calling it an addition.

photojournal.title: Two-image Mosaic of Saturn’s Rings
photojournal.reason: Voyager ring mosaic offers a geometric/profile lead, but perspective brightness does not solve the missing calibrated radius-indexed color source.

photojournal.title: Northern Hemisphere of Saturn
photojournal.reason: Voyager November 1980 Saturn northern cloud image is a separate epoch/footprint lead for the historical observing-set proposal.

photojournal.title: Triton Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Triton high-resolution mosaic fills between frames with lower-resolution observations; current controlled imagery already addresses the encounter, so compare actual support first.

photojournal.title: Mosaic of Saturn’s Rings
photojournal.reason: Underside Cassini-Division imagery is a ring-scattering observation lead; radial geometry and viewing-side calibration differ from face-on reflectance.

photojournal.title: Io – Southern Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: Io southern terminator photograph supplies shadow/terrain context at one geometry; do not derive a numeric height field from the press image.

photojournal.title: Voyager 1 Jupiter Southern Hemisphere Movie
photojournal.reason: Voyager sequence spans 17 Jupiter days; choose original dated maps/frames for existing controls rather than fabricate continuous surface animation.

photojournal.title: Io 2×2 Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Voyager four-image Io color mosaic is a 1979 baseline, conditional on original bands, registration and comparison with later epochs.

photojournal.title: Proposed Mars Polar Lander Landing Site (Flat Map)
photojournal.reason: Mars Polar Lander planned ellipse on Viking context is a historical targeting map, not proof of the actual landing position or new imagery.

photojournal.title: Outgoing Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: Mariner 10 outgoing Mercury hemisphere provides a 1974 historical observation, though current MESSENGER maps are the spatial baseline.

photojournal.title: Incoming Hemisphere – Enhanced Color
photojournal.reason: Recalibrated Mariner 10 enhanced color could add a distinct spectral comparison; native channels and processing must replace mineral claims inferred from RGB.

photojournal.title: NEAR’s First Whole-Eros Mosaic from Orbit
photojournal.reason: First orbital Eros mosaic is a dated four-frame polar observation; compare source footprints against selected global MSI maps.

photojournal.title: Eros Image Mosaic, Looking North
photojournal.reason: Eros crescent mosaic has roughly 35 m resolvable features and partial illumination; native frames may add a useful regional view after overlap checks.

photojournal.title: Mosaic of Mathilde
photojournal.reason: Four-frame Mathilde flyby mosaic is the same limited encounter family already used; no new coverage or better resolved source demonstrated.

photojournal.title: Galileo PPR Temperature Maps of Loki in October 1999
photojournal.reason: Galileo PPR maps of Loki's October 1999 eruption measure thermal behavior distinct from later JIRAM radiance; retain epoch and physical units.

photojournal.title: Europa’s Jupiter-Facing Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: Europa twelve-frame November 1999 mosaic has approximately 1 km pixels plus lower-resolution context; establish improvement over current CLEAR coverage.

photojournal.title: Temperature Map of Io’s Night Side
photojournal.reason: Io night-temperature mosaic combines November 1999 and February 2000; keep spurious-edge warning and separate encounters from one instantaneous map.

photojournal.title: Temperature Map of Pele, Io
photojournal.reason: Pele February 2000 infrared temperature overlay uses 1979 visible context; the thermal footprint must not inherit the background's apparent resolution or epoch.

photojournal.title: Mars Pathfinder “Filled Donut” Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Pathfinder filled-donut panorama includes a museum lander model and reprojection; not pure measured surface imagery, with Mars work deferred.

photojournal.title: MOLA Global Roughness Map of Mars
photojournal.reason: MOLA roughness uses 300 m baselines summarized over 35 km windows; distinct from height or regional slope, retained under deferred Mars scope.

photojournal.title: MOLA Global Map of Surface Gradients on Mars
photojournal.reason: MOLA regional gradients use 30 km baselines; record separately from the roughness statistic and defer Mars implementation.

photojournal.title: Mars Gravity Anomoly Map
photojournal.reason: Mars radio-science gravity anomaly is a numeric source lead overlapping the gravity family, not a new independent press-image measurement.

photojournal.title: Southern Hemisphere Storms
photojournal.reason: Cassini Jupiter southern-storm movie offers dated original frames; retain interval and common geometry instead of treating its still as a global map.

photojournal.title: High Resolution Globe of Jupiter
photojournal.reason: Cassini December 2000 globe was rendered from a cylindrical map; recover the underlying four-image map, not pixels from the rendered limb.

photojournal.title: Mosaic of Eros’ Northern Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: Eros polar display drapes imagery on a computer shape; original source frames or registered mosaic are required, not reverse projection of the press render.

photojournal.title: Mosaic of Eros’ Northern Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: June 2000 low-sun Eros view emphasizes small relief; useful regional imaging candidate with illumination retained, not albedo inferred from shadows.

photojournal.title: Southwest of the Big Crater (Mosaic)
photojournal.reason: Eight-image Eros crater-area mosaic from 50 km altitude may add regional detail; compare exact source pixels with the selected MSI base.

photojournal.title: The Southern Saddle (Mosaic)
photojournal.reason: Seven-image southern-saddle mosaic targets a specific regional structure; qualify footprint and registration without creating a separate photo panel.

photojournal.title: Global View of the Arctic Ocean
photojournal.reason: Radarsat Arctic sea-ice mosaic adds a broad radar/cryosphere lead; distinguish dated backscatter imagery from inferred motion or thickness.

photojournal.title: Color Mosaic of Olympus Mons
photojournal.reason: Viking Olympus Mons color mosaic is dated June 1978 regional imagery; Mars work remains deferred.

photojournal.title: Mars Digital Image Mosaic Globe
photojournal.reason: Rendered Mars DIM globe combines different-resolution monochrome and color inputs; original DIM maps are the source lead, not this globe image.

photojournal.title: Mars Orbiter Laser Altimiter (MOLA) Globe
photojournal.reason: MOLA globe is colorized shaded relief; future numeric-height work would use original elevations and datum, with Mars presently excluded.

photojournal.title: Atmospheric Motion in Jupiter’s Northern Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: Northern Jupiter motion plate reuses true/false-color Galileo time sequences; trace back to those observations rather than count new independent coverage.

photojournal.title: Jovian Ring System Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Galileo Jupiter ring mosaic measures strongly geometry-dependent scattered light; only a qualified radial/profile outcome fits the unchanged renderer.

photojournal.title: Mercury’s Southern Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: Mariner southern Mercury photomosaic is a historical imaging variant; compare native inputs with other Mariner mosaics and current MESSENGER coverage.

photojournal.title: Looking Along the Southern Hemisphere of Eros
photojournal.reason: September 2000 Eros stereo sequence gives southern context; potential regional registration evidence, not a standalone new global texture.

photojournal.title: A Road map for Eros
photojournal.reason: Four Eros reference-system illustrations explain coordinates but do not constitute four additional observed datasets; use authoritative frame definitions instead.

photojournal.title: Eros Map and Place Names
photojournal.reason: Eros map carries proposed historical names and acknowledged mosaic seams; current IAU features and seven MSI maps supersede it as the default source.

photojournal.title: Eros Closest Approach Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Low-altitude Eros closest-approach mosaic has potentially useful boulder/regolith detail; native camera/shape geometry and tiny footprint must be qualified.

photojournal.title: Color Mapping the Southern Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: Southern crater observation is part of a color sequence; compare original channels and common coverage with the shipped seven-band MSI maps.

photojournal.title: A Southern Hemisphere Overview
photojournal.reason: December 2000 southern Eros mosaic is south-up with terminator near the equator; preserve orientation and illuminated footprint in any regional addition.

photojournal.title: Morning on Chryse Planitia – Viking Lander 1 Camera 1 Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Viking 1 camera-1 morning panorama combines multiple days; local imaging and Mars scope remain deferred.

photojournal.title: Morning on Chryse Planitia – Viking Lander 1 Camera 2 Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Viking 1 camera-2 morning panorama is a different camera view, not a planetary map; retain that identity under deferred Mars scope.

photojournal.title: Afternoon on Chryse Planitia – Viking Lander 1 Camera 1 Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Viking 1 camera-1 afternoon mosaic differs in illumination from the morning set; no global dataset or present Mars implementation.

photojournal.title: Afternoon on Chryse Planitia – Viking Lander 1 Camera 2 Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Viking 1 camera-2 afternoon mosaic is the fourth local camera/time variant; not four independent global surveys.

photojournal.title: Radargram of Mars’ North Polar Layered Deposits with Topographic Map
photojournal.reason: MARSIS north-polar radargram is a subsurface track section paired with MOLA context, not a surface raster; Mars is deferred.

photojournal.title: Topographic Map of Chryse Planitia with Location of Possible Buried Basin
photojournal.reason: Chryse MOLA context marks radar tracks and an interpreted buried basin; original radar evidence, not the annotation, would support a later Mars study.

photojournal.title: Shaded Relief with Color as Height, California Mosaic
photojournal.reason: California SRTM colored relief points to native terrain; compare quantitative regional detail with current GEBCO, without importing the shaded RGB as heights.

photojournal.title: Nyiragongo Volcano, Congo, Map View with Lava, Landsat / ASTER / SRTM
photojournal.reason: Nyiragongo combines Landsat, ASTER and SRTM around a 2002 eruption; recover dated observations and distinguish mapped lava from background terrain.

photojournal.title: Shaded Relief with Color as Height, California Mosaic with Insets
photojournal.reason: California relief with insets repackages the terrain behind PIA03333; the insets do not create an independent elevation dataset.

photojournal.title: World in Mercator Projection, Shaded Relief and Colored Height
photojournal.reason: SRTM30 world relief is about 30-arcsecond sampling and colorized; current numeric GEBCO is preferable unless a specific measured discrepancy is established.

photojournal.title: SRTM Data Release for Eurasia, Index Map and Colored Height
photojournal.reason: Eurasia SRTM release index is a route to original elevation tiles, not a height grid itself; assess native regional benefit over current terrain.

photojournal.title: The MGS MOC Wide Angle Map of Mars
photojournal.reason: MGS MOC wide-angle global map is a distinct Mars imagery family, recorded under the existing Mars exclusion.

photojournal.title: Southern Hemisphere Neutron Map
photojournal.reason: Odyssey southern high-energy neutron counts are sensitive to shallow hydrogen; keep counts and interpreted hydrogen distinct if Mars work reopens.

photojournal.title: Global Map, High-Energy Neutrons
photojournal.reason: First-week global neutron map has background-subtracted count rates and limited survey duration; not direct water-ice percentage.

photojournal.title: Southern Hemisphere Polygonal Patterned Ground
photojournal.reason: Southern patterned-ground image is geomorphic evidence, not proof that the Earth periglacial analogy applies; Mars is deferred.

photojournal.title: Shaded Relief Mosaic of Umnak Island, Aleutian Islands, Alaska
photojournal.reason: Umnak AIRSAR shaded relief leads to a regional elevation product; inspect native accuracy, date and detail relative to GEBCO before selecting.

photojournal.title: Opportunity Traverse Map, Sol 656
photojournal.reason: Opportunity Sol 656 traverse annotates an existing orbital mosaic; route history is distinct from new observed map pixels.

photojournal.title: Spirit Traverse Map, Sol 680
photojournal.reason: Spirit Sol 680 traverse is historical path content on MOC imagery; current Mars exclusion remains.

photojournal.title: Global Map of Ganymede
photojournal.reason: Ganymede calibrated/photometrically normalized Galileo-Voyager base is the source family already used; compare exact release versions rather than announce missing global coverage.

photojournal.title: Global Map of Epithermal Neutrons
photojournal.reason: Epithermal neutron map is a hydrogen-sensitive count-rate field; original units and calibration required, with Mars implementation deferred.

photojournal.title: Global Map of Thermal Neutrons
photojournal.reason: Thermal neutrons respond to both hydrogen and CO₂ frost; this is a separate quantity from the epithermal map, retained under deferred scope.

photojournal.title: Polar Maps of Thermal and Epithermal Neutrons
photojournal.reason: Polar thermal/epithermal panels are projections of related neutron measurements, not four independent compositional surveys.

photojournal.title: HEND Maps of Fast Neutrons
photojournal.reason: HEND fast-neutron maps provide a separate energy response and background treatment; Mars work deferred with identity preserved.

photojournal.title: HEND Maps of Epithermal Neutrons
photojournal.reason: HEND epithermal maps overlap the neutron science family but differ by instrument/energy response; do not collapse them into direct ice abundance.

photojournal.title: Anti-Atlas Mountains, Morocco
photojournal.reason: ASTER Anti-Atlas spectral imagery is a regional geological/vegetation imaging lead, not the Saturn moon Atlas or a ready mineral abundance grid.

photojournal.title: Partially-Exhumed Crater in Northern Terra Meridiani: Mosaic of M04-01289, E17-01676, and M21-01646
photojournal.reason: Three MOC narrow-angle images of a partly exhumed crater form a regional Mars mosaic; original IDs are identified and scope remains deferred.

photojournal.title: Arsia Mons Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Arsia Mons daytime THEMIS infrared mosaic is distinct from visible imagery but needs native radiometric interpretation; Mars deferred.

photojournal.title: South Hemisphere Gullies
photojournal.reason: Southern crater gullies at 1.5 m/pixel are local morphology; historical liquid-flow wording is not accepted as a current measurement claim.

photojournal.title: Map of Martian Iron at Mid-Latitudes
photojournal.reason: Odyssey GRS mid-latitude iron map is a genuine elemental-data lead, distinct from visible red color; Mars work deferred.

photojournal.title: Map of Martian Polar Hydrogen
photojournal.reason: GRS north-polar hydrogen map has an ice interpretation tied to region/depth; original numeric retrieval and uncertainty needed under reopened scope.

photojournal.title: Map of Martian Potassium at Mid-Latitudes
photojournal.reason: GRS potassium abundance is a separate elemental measurement; preserve it in the ledger despite no current Mars implementation.

photojournal.title: Map of Martian Silicon at Mid-Latitudes
photojournal.reason: GRS silicon abundance is distinct from iron/potassium maps; original units and broad footprint are required for any later Mars work.

photojournal.title: Map of Martian Thorium at Mid-Latitudes
photojournal.reason: GRS thorium trace-element map offers another scientific quantity; press colors are not calibrated concentration values and Mars is deferred.

photojournal.title: Natural Color Mosaic of North America
photojournal.reason: MISR North America cloud-free mosaic mixes imagery with shaded-relief inputs; compare actual spectral/photographic gain over Blue Marble and separate injected relief.

photojournal.title: Cloud Height Maps for Hurricanes Frances and Ivan
photojournal.reason: MISR hurricane cloud-top heights are measured regional retrievals from two dates; original height grids and cloud masks could fit a prepared observation view.

photojournal.title: Water Mass Map from Neutron Spectrometer
photojournal.reason: Neutron-derived water-mass map gives a lower limit for the upper metre, not an exact surface ice fraction; retain as a deferred Mars opportunity.

photojournal.title: Map of Hills on the Horizon
photojournal.reason: Spirit hill/context map combines orbital and descent imagery for local positioning; not an independent whole-body dataset.

photojournal.title: Map of Moessbauer Placement
photojournal.reason: Microscopic soil topography after Mössbauer contact is millimetre-scale instrument evidence, not a planetary elevation layer; Mars also excluded.

photojournal.title: Southern Hemisphere in Ultraviolet
photojournal.reason: Cassini May 2004 UV Saturn image adds a dated band observation; clouds/aerosols and gas brightness need their UV interpretation retained.

photojournal.title: Hematite Abundance Map at Echo
photojournal.reason: Mini-TES hematite retrieval around Opportunity's Echo position is a local measurement; not global Meridiani abundance and Mars deferred.

photojournal.title: Spirit’s View on Sol 93 (cylindrical)
photojournal.reason: Spirit Sol 93 navigation-camera cylindrical panorama is a local viewpoint; preserve date and defer Mars work.

photojournal.title: Spirit’s View on Sol 100 (cylindrical)
photojournal.reason: Spirit Sol 100 panorama is a separate rover epoch but not a body-fixed global map; Mars excluded.

photojournal.title: Spirit’s View on Sol 101 (cylindrical)
photojournal.reason: Spirit Sol 101 Missoula approach panorama is local camera content; no surface-photo panel is being reintroduced.

photojournal.title: MSIP: Multinational Research in the Southern Hemisphere
photojournal.reason: Student-selected southern Mars investigation points to a regional observation; no independent global data product established and Mars is deferred.

photojournal.title: Temperature Map, “Bonneville Crater”
photojournal.reason: Bonneville Mini-TES five-time temperature sequence is a local diurnal experiment, not five global maps; Mars scope remains deferred.

photojournal.title: Temperature Map, “Bonneville Crater” (10:15 a.m.)
photojournal.reason: Bonneville 10:15 local-time thermal frame is the first member of PIA05927's sequence; preserve its individual timestamp.

photojournal.title: Temperature Map, “Bonneville Crater” (11:49 a.m.)
photojournal.reason: Bonneville 11:49 local-time thermal frame is the second member, with shared geometry and retrieval assumptions.

photojournal.title: Temperature Map, “Bonneville Crater” (1:35 p.m.)
photojournal.reason: Bonneville 13:35 thermal frame is the third diurnal sample; no independent survey or global coverage is implied.

photojournal.title: Temperature Map, “Bonneville Crater” (2:35 p.m.)
photojournal.reason: Bonneville 14:35 thermal frame is the fourth local measurement; implementation remains outside current Mars scope.

photojournal.title: Temperature Map, “Bonneville Crater” (4:39 p.m.)
photojournal.reason: Bonneville 16:39 thermal frame completes the five-time local series; grouping would preserve times if Mars scope reopened.

photojournal.title: Hebes Chasma Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Hebes Chasma Odyssey mosaic is regional canyon imagery; original footprint/units would need qualification in a later Mars task.

photojournal.title: Endurance Road Map
photojournal.reason: Endurance road map combines orbital, descent and rover cameras with a route annotation; source observations and path data are different products.

photojournal.title: Phoebe Hi-Resolution Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Phoebe six-image close-encounter mosaic may offer regional detail beyond the selected global view; cross-match native frames and current texture support.

photojournal.title: Atlas Found!
photojournal.reason: Atlas is a tiny moving moon in a 112-image sequence; not resolved surface-map coverage or a reason to invent an Atlas texture.

photojournal.title: The Atlas Ring
photojournal.reason: New narrow-ring observation near Atlas is a source lead for radial support, not calibrated opacity/color; require native geometry and a valid profile.

photojournal.reason: Titan October 2004 28-image footprint set could support a dated ISS comparison with original haze treatment and measured regional coverage.

photojournal.title: Titan Mosaic: December 2004

photojournal.title: Titan Mosaic – Feb 2005

photojournal.title: Enceladus Mosaic

photojournal.title: Tracing Surface Features on Titan–Mosaic

photojournal.title: Titan Mosaic — East of Xanadu
photojournal.reason: East-of-Xanadu mosaic combines narrow- and wide-angle imaging with different resolution; keep their individual spatial support.

photojournal.title: Zooming In On Enceladus (Mosaic)
photojournal.reason: Twenty-one-frame Enceladus July 2005 mosaic is a potential local-detail source; compare exact observations with the newer selected global release.

photojournal.title: Martian City Map
photojournal.reason: Mars polar polygons resemble a city map only visually; no cities or new categorical map are implied, and Mars is deferred.

photojournal.title: Phoebe Temperature Maps
photojournal.reason: Phoebe CIRS montage is a local-time temperature sequence with unobserved areas; recover numeric maps instead of merging them into a simultaneous globe.

photojournal.title: Titan Map

photojournal.title: Enceladus Temperature Map
photojournal.reason: Enceladus south-polar CIRS heat observation is distinct from the predicted solar-temperature panel; observed and modeled fields must remain separate.

photojournal.title: Atlas, Pandora and Janus
photojournal.reason: Rings-and-moons context photograph includes unresolved or tiny moons; it does not supply mapped surfaces or new orbital facts beyond native navigation sources.

photojournal.title: A Glimpse of Atlas
photojournal.reason: Atlas barely resolved disc and overexposed ring edge cannot support a calibrated surface texture or precise radial reflectance profile.

photojournal.title: Spirit Traverse Map
photojournal.reason: Spirit traverse locates the Santa Anita panorama and represents route history, not a new global map; Mars deferred.

photojournal.title: ‘Endurance’ All Around (cylindrical)
photojournal.reason: Opportunity Sol 171 Endurance panorama is a local cylindrical projection; camera orientation is not body-fixed longitude.

photojournal.title: Hilly Surroundings (cylindrical)

photojournal.title: Valles Marineris Mosaic
photojournal.reason: Odyssey Valles Marineris mosaic is a regional imaging lead; current Mars exclusion remains without losing the source record.

photojournal.title: Tyrrhena Patera Mosaic

photojournal.title: Iapetus Temperature Map

photojournal.title: Iapetus Temperature Variation Map
photojournal.reason: Iapetus temperature-versus-local-time plot compares measurements with a thermal-inertia model; suitable as qualified chart data, not an additional spatial map.

photojournal.title: Digital Elevation Map of Spirit’s Trek
photojournal.reason: Spirit trek elevation map combines orbital height and path context; a regional Mars route product, not a new global DEM.

photojournal.title: Mosaic of River Channel and Ridge Area on Titan

photojournal.title: Spirit Traverse Map, Sol 404
photojournal.reason: Spirit Sol 404 traverse marks a historical 4.143 km path on orbital imagery; path data and background pixels are separate.

photojournal.title: Opportunity Traverse Map, Sol 383
photojournal.reason: Opportunity Sol 383 traverse records a 2.801 km route; Mars scope remains deferred rather than treating the annotated map as new imaging.

photojournal.title: Embedded Atlas

photojournal.title: Rhea: Polar View
photojournal.reason: Rhea south-polar crater close-up may add local photographic detail; compare its original frame support with the selected 417 m global mosaic.

photojournal.title: Enceladus: North and South (Northern Polar Projection)

photojournal.title: Enceladus: North and South (Southern Polar Projection)

photojournal.title: Enceladus: Global Patterns of Fracture (Northern Polar Projection)

photojournal.title: Enceladus: Global Patterns of Fracture (Southern Polar Projection)

photojournal.title: Map of Phoebe — December 2005

photojournal.title: Map of Dione — December 2005

photojournal.title: Map of Enceladus — December 2005

photojournal.title: Map of Iapetus — December 2005

photojournal.title: Map of Rhea — December 2005

photojournal.title: Map of Tethys — December 2005

photojournal.title: Cassini’s Best Maps of Jupiter (Cylindrical Map)

photojournal.title: Cassini’s Best Maps of Jupiter (North Polar Map)

photojournal.title: Cassini’s Best Maps of Jupiter (South Polar Map)

photojournal.title: Phoebe: Cartographic Projections (Mercator Projection)

photojournal.title: Phoebe: Cartographic Projections (North Polar Map)

photojournal.title: Phoebe: Cartographic Projections (South Polar Map)

photojournal.title: Huygens Titan Mosaic #2

proposals.title: Bennu: heat storage, roughness and predicted temperatures
proposals.current: Bennu has albedo, monochrome, four reflected-light bands, spectral color and elevation. No thermal view is present at the pinned revision.
proposals.result: Eight global maps: OTES and OVIRS thermal inertia, OTES and OVIRS thermal roughness, and four OTES-based temperature extremes at the nearest and farthest points from the Sun. Group related maps with the existing arrow selector.
proposals.evidence: The collection inventory lists 16 products: eight global maps, four site-specific thermal-inertia maps and four site meshes. Full scans of both global inertia FITS tables found 48,958/49,152 finite values for OTES (99.61%) and 48,273/49,152 for OVIRS (98.21%). These are facet counts, not area-weighted coverage. Each file is 1,189,440 bytes.
proposals.work: Prepare facet values and uncertainty on the current surface; preserve missing values; retain the source instrument and model identity. No renderer change is expected.
proposals.limit: Thermal inertia is a fitted measure of resistance to heating and cooling. Temperature extremes are predictions, not simultaneous observations. The FITS names a v034 SPO source shape; the displayed Bennu uses OLA v20. Verify transfer without replacing the display mesh. The OVIRS file incorrectly says OTES in INSTRUME; its product name and companion record identify OVIRS. Roughness and temperature payloads still need their own numeric checks.
proposals.checks: Compare decoded samples against the source FITS; measure area-weighted coverage after mesh transfer; check seams, poles, picking and the instrument selector. Resolve the OVIRS header conflict in the source record.

proposals.title: Bennu: hydrated minerals and carbon-bearing material
proposals.current: The current spectral color is a MapCam visible/near-infrared composite, not an OVIRS hydration or carbon-band map.
proposals.result: Separate maps of the 2.74 µm absorption and the 3.2–3.6 µm band area. They show spectral signatures that are absent from the existing MapCam color maps.
proposals.evidence: Downloaded and scanned the two native FITS products. Each contains 196,608 rows and is 4,728,960 bytes. The OH product has 367 negative values at the missing-data floor; the carbon-band product has 370 negative values, so negativity alone is not a safe generic mask. The FITS shape and row count agree with the detailed-survey README's roughly 200,000-facet v020 SPC model.
proposals.work: A larger preparation task than thermal inertia. Use the source FITS layout, retain archive discrepancies as evidence, and qualify the scientific quantity before adding a surface view.
proposals.limit: The OH XML says 49,152 records; the FITS has four times as many. Its filename says 2.7 µm while the README specifies a measurement at 2.74 µm. The XML says percent but native values are around 0.14 and the FITS unit is BAND_DEPTH: establish the scale explicitly before labeling. Carbonates and organics both contribute to the 3.2–3.6 µm feature; do not label it organic abundance. Resolve fill values, source-frame transfer and uncertainty before release.
proposals.checks: Resolve fraction versus percent using the native documentation and an independent numeric sample. Preserve the -9999 sentinel while investigating the three additional negative carbon-band values. Check source-shape registration. Include the OTES 350 cm⁻¹ band only if emission-angle bias can be bounded; otherwise retain its exclusion.

proposals.title: Ceres: hydrogen and iron
proposals.current: Existing Ceres composition views use VIR mineral absorptions and band centres. No GRaND map is selected.
proposals.result: Two chemically distinct global measurements from Dawn GRaND, with their uncertainty columns.
proposals.evidence: Native labels and hydrogen table inspected. The products use 110 approximately equal-area cells. Hydrogen is water-equivalent hydrogen by mass; iron is mass fraction. Measurements were collected in the low-altitude mapping orbit in 2015–2016.
proposals.work: Small numeric tables fit the existing prepared surface lane. Keep the coarse footprint and uncertainty visible in the description; do not produce crater-scale detail.
proposals.limit: The effective resolution is roughly 600 km FWHM. Twenty-degree cells are sampling, not independent resolved terrain. Hydrogen does not uniquely measure surface ice, and a water-equivalent value is not an ice-fraction map.
proposals.checks: Independently check table units and uncertainty columns; compare prepared cell values and boundaries against the native table. Keep the approximately 600 km footprint explicit.

proposals.title: Vesta: hydrogen and iron signal
proposals.current: The current Vesta package has imagery, spectral ratios and elevation. No GRaND measurement is selected.
proposals.result: Hydrogen and corrected iron gamma-ray signal; neutron absorption is a possible later addition.
proposals.evidence: Hydrogen has 16,200 two-degree cells, µg/g values and uncertainty. Effective spatial resolution is about 300 km FWHM. The corrected iron table is a count-rate product, not a directly measured iron mass fraction.
proposals.work: Reuse the Ceres GRaND reader while preserving different units and frame conventions. The renderer can remain unchanged.
proposals.limit: The release uses Claudia Double Prime; the current body uses Claudia. A documented offline coordinate conversion is required. Do not adopt the archive's preliminary iron conversion without its stated limitations. Two-degree sampling does not mean two-degree resolution.
proposals.checks: Verify Claudia Double Prime to Claudia coordinates against independent landmarks. Check hydrogen values and uncertainty, iron count-rate units, missing cells and the approximately 300 km effective resolution.

proposals.title: Ceres and Vesta: gravity, anomalies and geoid
proposals.current: These gravity fields are not selected surface datasets in the three current packages.
proposals.result: Prepare Dawn's published gravity, Bouguer anomaly, geoid and associated errors for Ceres and Vesta. Give each physical quantity a clear label within one related group per body.
proposals.evidence: Ceres and Vesta native map labels describe 360 × 181 grids, including radial acceleration and error products. Bennu's native label specifies 196,608 facet records with normalized anomaly and mGal columns. The source overview explains comparison with a uniform-density shape.
proposals.work: Decode the existing numeric grids at preparation time. Use plain labels such as Gravity variation, with mission attribution and a concise explanation of the reference model.
proposals.limit: These are model-derived fields. Grid spacing does not equal resolving power; harmonic degree, reference surface, density assumption, scale/offset, longitude and uncertainty all matter. An anomaly is not a direct map of hidden caverns or mineral abundance.
proposals.checks: Read grid scale, offset, longitude, reference radius, density assumption and harmonic degree. Verify numeric samples against a separate decoder and keep uncertainty separate from anomaly. A grid cell is not the model's effective resolution.

proposals.title: Bennu: gravity anomaly on the observed shape
proposals.current: These gravity fields are not selected surface datasets in the three current packages.
proposals.result: Prepare the published Bennu Bouguer anomaly, retaining its physical units and uniform-density reference model. Keep it separate from Dawn's regular-grid importer.
proposals.evidence: Ceres and Vesta native map labels describe 360 × 181 grids, including radial acceleration and error products. Bennu's native label specifies 196,608 facet records with normalized anomaly and mGal columns. The source overview explains comparison with a uniform-density shape.
proposals.work: Decode the existing numeric grids at preparation time. Use plain labels such as Gravity variation, with mission attribution and a concise explanation of the reference model.
proposals.limit: These are model-derived fields. Grid spacing does not equal resolving power; harmonic degree, reference surface, density assumption, scale/offset, longitude and uncertainty all matter. An anomaly is not a direct map of hidden caverns or mineral abundance.
proposals.checks: Check all 196,608 facet rows, missing values and the distinction between normalized anomaly and mGal. Establish source-shape registration without inventing subsurface structures.

proposals.title: Eros: 334 mapped pond locations
proposals.current: Eros currently has IAU named features and seven reflected-light maps. The pond catalogue is not included.
proposals.result: A scientific feature catalogue of smooth deposits, placed through the existing surface-feature contract.
proposals.evidence: The native label declares 334 records with pond number, IAU_EROS Cartesian coordinates, north latitude, east longitude and diameter in kilometres. The bundle description says the locations were transferred from MSI pixels to the Gaskell SPC shape with SBMT; frame constants are identified in eros_alex.tpc.
proposals.work: Import the feature table into the existing prepared feature system. Useful and understandable, but smaller than the multi-map proposals above.
proposals.limit: Ponds are smooth deposits of fine material, not liquid water. The source warns that several catalogue circles can belong to one continuous deposit, and detection is biased by image resolution, especially below 30 m. Diameters are characteristic sizes of generally noncircular features. Catalogue IDs must not be presented as IAU names.
proposals.checks: Import all 334 catalogue records with stable research IDs, coordinates and characteristic diameter. Validate the IAU_EROS frame and size units. Keep multiple circles belonging to one deposit distinguishable; never call them 334 separate ponds or IAU names.

proposals.title: Mimas: relative reflectivity
proposals.current: The source bundle already supplies Mimas's shape and radius map, but its relative-albedo product is not selected. Dione, Rhea, Tethys and Phoebe already have similar reflectivity views.
proposals.result: Add the SPC relative-albedo GeoTIFF beside the existing photos and elevation.
proposals.evidence: The native mimas_albedo_g.xml describes a 2,222 × 1,111 unitless GeoTIFF associated with the SPC topography.
proposals.work: A bounded texture addition using the same source family. No need to change geometry. Supporting image-count or uncertainty rasters are secondary opportunities, not new physical measurements.
proposals.limit: This is relative albedo, not absolute reflectance. Read its actual geotransform and missing-data conventions; the current radius map already has a documented narrow edge gap.
proposals.checks: Inspect native GeoTIFF extent, relative scaling, geotransform and no-data before preparation. Check the known edge gap and fixed geometry. Compare with the same source-family views on Dione, Rhea, Tethys and Phoebe.

proposals.title: Moon: nine Kaguya reflected-light bands
proposals.current: Kaguya mineral, grain-size, iron and maturity products are already selected. The nine measured MI spectral bands are the remaining distinct addition.
proposals.result: Add a single reflected-light group with nine wavelength choices and JAXA / Kaguya MI attribution.
proposals.evidence: The USGS audit inspected nine 16-bit spectral products. Their coverage is approximately 65°S to 65°N, wider than the derived mineral maps but not polar coverage.
proposals.work: Read the native scale and invalid-value rules, reduce the bands together on the same grid, and preserve their common validity mask. Keep these measured bands separate from fitted mineral products.
proposals.limit: Nine bands are nine wavelength samples, not nine minerals. Verify photometric treatment and JAXA reuse terms. Do not repeat the already shipped derived maps.
proposals.checks: Independent source-to-prepared values, common footprint, wavelength order, band switching and byte budget.

proposals.title: Moon: improve existing photography and height sampling
proposals.current: The current Moon uses coarser LROC morphology and LOLA inputs; its surface geometry stays fixed.
proposals.result: Replace an existing prepared map only where finer input produces visible or numerical improvement at the existing display budget.
proposals.evidence: The audit verified the 59 m merged DEM within ±60°, 118 m LOLA and 100 m WAC alternatives. PIA18138 supplies a separate north-pole imaging lead, not proof that the whole Moon has that detail.
proposals.work: Run a matched preparation at the present asset dimensions, then compare a bounded larger texture level if the existing contract supports it. Record improvement per delivered byte.
proposals.limit: No terrain displacement, mesh refinement or extra duplicate dataset row. Preserve regional coverage and the difference between source sampling and actual resolution.
proposals.checks: Matched close-up samples, poles, numeric heights, seams, source values and delivered byte counts; reject a replacement that gives no useful gain.

proposals.title: Europa: expand registered infrared coverage
proposals.current: Two registered NIMS products supply the current infrared composite. Other composition datasets already exist and should remain distinct.
proposals.result: Use additional qualified NIMS observations to improve measured coverage and add a water-ice or hydrate signature only when the archived quantity supports it.
proposals.evidence: The expanded USGS listing contains 794 TIFF URLs, including alternate processing products. Photojournal identifies trailing-hemisphere, Tyre and Manannán observations worth tracing back to original cubes.
proposals.work: Deduplicate by observation and processing version, join geometry and quality products, measure incremental surface coverage, and retain wavelength, observation epoch and calibration lineage.
proposals.limit: 794 files do not mean 794 observations. The Manannán press overlay is regional and is not a quantitative abundance raster. Do not merge incompatible brightness scales or sharpen NIMS with SSI detail.
proposals.checks: A per-observation coverage table, independent band samples, geometry landmarks, explicit overlap rules and comparison against the existing two-product baseline.

proposals.title: Callisto: expand registered infrared coverage
proposals.current: Two NIMS products supply the existing infrared view.
proposals.result: Increase measured infrared coverage and assess additional water-ice spectral information through the current surface-data controls.
proposals.evidence: The USGS release lists 93 TIFF URLs. PIA00844 is a Callisto product despite its supplied Ganymede target tag; PIA01079 shows another NIMS/SSI comparison.
proposals.work: Identify independent observations, read native units and masks, and compare their measured footprints with the selected products before choosing additions.
proposals.limit: Separate wavelength images, browse products and processing versions do not each create a dataset. Preserve coarse spectral resolution and observation-time differences.
proposals.checks: Record net new measured area, sample original cube values independently, and inspect seams, orientation and missing areas on the fixed body.

proposals.title: Ryugu: thermal-corrected infrared spectra
proposals.current: Ryugu already has thermal inertia, visible spectral slope, monochrome, enhanced color, elevation and a close-up. Those are not new opportunities.
proposals.result: Investigate an infrared absorption map using the 2026 NIRS3 thermal-excess-removed release, distinct from the existing visible spectral slope.
proposals.evidence: The collection inventories contain 107 spectrum products and 109 geometry products. A native LBLX sample describes 128 channels × 2,695 spectra, a corresponding standard-deviation array, and an estimated-temperature array. This is an actual calibrated numeric release with geometry, not a gallery of pictures.
proposals.work: A source-reduction PR after a bounded coverage pilot. Reuse the existing surface renderer, but budget substantial preparation and qualification work.
proposals.limit: There is no ready global hydration raster in this bundle. Quality filtering, geometry association, thermal correction limits and footprint coverage must be established. A source release date is not the observation date.
proposals.checks: Join the 107 spectrum products and 109 geometry products by identifiers, not row order. Independently check channel wavelengths, thermal correction, standard deviations and valid footprint coverage. Release a map only if the inferred signature survives these checks.

proposals.title: Itokawa: more AMICA wavelengths
proposals.current: The current ten-frame v-band mosaic already uses this source family and has 84.26% sampled display-mesh coverage. It is not a new backplane discovery.
proposals.result: Investigate additional AMICA filters using the archived geometry backplanes.
proposals.evidence: The archive contains the AMICA observation and backplane bundles. The body ledger records successful selected paired exposures and other exposures rejected by the existing brightness or registration limits.
proposals.work: Survey same-pointing filter sets and demonstrate worthwhile registered coverage before committing to a large PR.
proposals.limit: Do not imply matching coverage in every band, reuse rejected exposures without new evidence, or relax registration tolerances to fill gaps. The separate native SBMT comparison has a documented unresolved one-pixel issue; the controlled-DDR production route is separate.
proposals.checks: Compare co-pointed filters and exposure/registration residuals against the current ten v-band frames. Report coverage per filter and common coverage before selecting a band set. Backplane availability alone does not repair the existing rejected exposures.

proposals.title: Ceres: qualified Urvara and crater close-ups
proposals.current: The current Ceres imagery is global; this would be an explicitly regional close-up.
proposals.result: A controlled high-resolution mosaic of Urvara crater, with separate products for different source-resolution ranges.
proposals.evidence: The native label describes a 57,573 × 40,282 mosaic resampled to 5 m/pixel from 1,583 images. The method document describes source imaging at about 3.5–20 m/pixel and a mapped region from 128°W to 93°W, 59°S to 35°S.
proposals.work: Prepare a bounded regional raster while retaining clear coverage. Lower priority for the user's preference for broadly useful coverage.
proposals.limit: It covers one basin, not the whole body. Five-metre output sampling is not uniform five-metre resolved detail. A generic radius description in the image label is inconsistent with the photographic product; use the explicit mosaic method record.
proposals.checks: Start with the controlled Urvara product. Treat Occator, Vinalia, Dantu and Haulani images as separate leads until their native registration and incremental detail are demonstrated. Compare output against global imagery at the same camera and budget; do not label resampled 5 m pixels as uniform 5 m detail.

proposals.title: Ceres: millimetre observations
proposals.current: No ALMA dataset is selected in Ceres's current surface controls.
proposals.result: A different wavelength range using the archived ALMA images, spectra and light curves.
proposals.evidence: The bundle and data inventory were read; the data collection separates images, imaging parameters, light curves and spectra.
proposals.work: A bounded native-product inspection before any surface proposal. Prefer the ready derived global products above.
proposals.limit: This audit has not decoded or registered its image payloads. Treat it as an observation lead, not a verified global temperature map. Spatial resolution, dates and instrumental beam must be checked first.
proposals.checks: Inspect the actual image, beam, epoch, calibration and geometry records. Prove whether a supported surface map or existing-chart observation is possible. Stop at an evidence-backed ledger update if neither is supported.

proposals.title: Small bodies: reconcile diameters and albedos
proposals.current: NEOWISE is already referenced for Amycus, Echeclus, Elatus, Okyrhoe and Thereus. Many radar target bodies already exist. A catalogue must be joined against existing object identities before counting additions.
proposals.result: Join NEOWISE, radiometric, occultation and radar compilations to existing object IDs; update only demonstrated gaps or better-supported measurements.
proposals.evidence: Latest discovered bundle versions include NEOWISE v2, LCDB v4 and occultations v4. Their inventories were read. Several are a handful of large tables, so product counts are not body counts.
proposals.work: A substantial facts PR is possible, using published uncertainties and an explicit source-selection policy. It adds scientific information rather than surface textures.
proposals.limit: This audit did not compute a row-level join against every existing body fact or adjudicate conflicting measurements. There is no verified number of new bodies or corrected facts yet. Old optical, radiometric and radar estimates are not interchangeable, and migration dates do not make observations new.
proposals.checks: Produce a row-level before/after fact ledger with method, epoch, uncertainty and source. Keep radiometric diameters separate from resolved shape dimensions. Do not announce a new-body count before the join.

proposals.title: Small bodies: measured rotation periods and light curves
proposals.current: NEOWISE is already referenced for Amycus, Echeclus, Elatus, Okyrhoe and Thereus. Many radar target bodies already exist. A catalogue must be joined against existing object identities before counting additions.
proposals.result: Reconcile published rotation periods and their quality codes; retain selected measured light curves only where existing chart content can present them faithfully.
proposals.evidence: Latest discovered bundle versions include NEOWISE v2, LCDB v4 and occultations v4. Their inventories were read. Several are a handful of large tables, so product counts are not body counts.
proposals.work: A substantial facts PR is possible, using published uncertainties and an explicit source-selection policy. It adds scientific information rather than surface textures.
proposals.limit: This audit did not compute a row-level join against every existing body fact or adjudicate conflicting measurements. There is no verified number of new bodies or corrected facts yet. Old optical, radiometric and radar estimates are not interchangeable, and migration dates do not make observations new.
proposals.checks: Handle aliases, synodic versus sidereal periods, period ambiguities and observation epochs. Preserve existing scene motion unless a separately justified source-backed fact change requires it; this proposal does not redesign motion.

proposals.title: Small bodies: masses, densities and binary properties
proposals.current: NEOWISE is already referenced for Amycus, Echeclus, Elatus, Okyrhoe and Thereus. Many radar target bodies already exist. A catalogue must be joined against existing object identities before counting additions.
proposals.result: Improve existing physical facts with published masses, densities, binary parameters and occultation size constraints, including their uncertainties.
proposals.evidence: Latest discovered bundle versions include NEOWISE v2, LCDB v4 and occultations v4. Their inventories were read. Several are a handful of large tables, so product counts are not body counts.
proposals.work: A substantial facts PR is possible, using published uncertainties and an explicit source-selection policy. It adds scientific information rather than surface textures.
proposals.limit: This audit did not compute a row-level join against every existing body fact or adjudicate conflicting measurements. There is no verified number of new bodies or corrected facts yet. Old optical, radiometric and radar estimates are not interchangeable, and migration dates do not make observations new.
proposals.checks: Resolve object/component IDs and correlated quantities. A binary-system mass is not an individual component mass. Do not derive precise density from incompatible size and mass estimates or turn an occultation chord into a surface map.

proposals.title: Asteroid spectral libraries and taxonomy
proposals.current: Potential additional scientific content; no claim that every target or classification is absent from cssEarth.
proposals.result: Source-backed whole-object spectra and spectral classifications across many asteroids.
proposals.evidence: MITHNEOS has 771 data products in its collection inventory. SMASS, SMASS II, S3OS2, PRIMASS and several targeted IRTF releases are also present and separately catalogued.
proposals.work: Join archive target IDs to existing bodies, retain spectra and calibration records, and then choose a bounded content addition.
proposals.limit: A disc-integrated spectrum does not locate minerals on a surface. A taxonomic class is not a measured mineral percentage. Plot and catalogue presentation compatibility requires a separate design check; this is not a ready surface-map PR.
proposals.checks: Join target identifiers, normalization wavelength, units, telluric masks, error arrays and observing dates. Separate taxonomy systems and whole-object reflectance spectra. Verify the existing prepared chart contract before adding content; no spatial mineral map follows from a disc-integrated spectrum.

proposals.title: Asteroids: source-backed family membership
proposals.current: The archive has several family and discovery compilations; a row-level comparison against current object facts has not been done.
proposals.result: Add or correct membership and discovery facts for existing objects where identifiers and the published classification agree.
proposals.evidence: Nesvorny HCM, Zappalà, Mothé-Diniz and high-inclination family bundles were found in the PDS4 tree.
proposals.work: Retain each catalogue's method and version, distinguish dynamical membership from spectral type, and document conflicting assignments rather than silently combining them.
proposals.limit: This is facts content, not a new scene, orbit layout or claim of shared composition. No verified number of additions yet.
proposals.checks: Review joined and unmatched rows, aliases, family parent IDs and exact source references. Keep uncertain or conflicting memberships qualified.

proposals.title: Small bodies: measured colors, phase curves and polarization
proposals.current: These catalogue families contain whole-object measurements; the audit has not established which individual facts or charts are missing.
proposals.result: Add selected measured photometric facts or prepared charts that answer a clear question about an existing body.
proposals.evidence: PDS4 contains asteroid, satellite and TNO colors, phase relations, polarization, and radar echo spectra.
proposals.work: Join IDs and record bandpass, geometry, epoch, normalization, uncertainty and calibration. Separate radar echo measurements from optical reflectance.
proposals.limit: Do not derive a new surface tint or lighting law from an unrelated whole-disc measurement. Renderer and lighting changes are outside this proposal.
proposals.checks: Use independent table samples and source plots. Verify chart compatibility first; retain a source decision if the existing content contract cannot display the quantity.

proposals.title: Eros: qualify X-ray, gamma-ray and infrared composition data
proposals.current: Gaspra and Ida NIMS are already recorded as unresolved in the body ledgers. Eros's existing seven MSI bands do not provide X-ray elemental maps.
proposals.result: Establish whether NEAR XRS, GRS or NIS can support a distinct elemental or spectral map with useful measured coverage.
proposals.evidence: The NEAR XRS collection has calibrated observations including level-3 directories; the scan did not find a ready global element raster. Galileo NIMS bundles contain calibrated point-perspective spectral cubes.
proposals.work: Keep as research candidates. Reopen the specific recorded blockers only with new evidence.
proposals.limit: Registration, footprint geometry, calibration and coverage remain substantial work. Gaspra has a pre-existing calibration-source discrepancy; Ida's current false-color coverage is only 17.2% of the display mesh. These are not replacements for the broadly covered recommendations above.
proposals.checks: Keep instrument footprints, solar excitation/calibration, units and uncertainty. Inventory level-3 products before raw reduction. Do not count the already shipped seven MSI bands as this addition.

proposals.title: Gaspra and Ida: resolve the existing NIMS blockers
proposals.current: Gaspra and Ida NIMS are already recorded as unresolved in the body ledgers. Eros's existing seven MSI bands do not provide X-ray elemental maps.
proposals.result: A bounded qualification PR resolving the recorded calibration and geometry issues in the NIMS cubes; a measured regional view is conditional on that result.
proposals.evidence: The NEAR XRS collection has calibrated observations including level-3 directories; the scan did not find a ready global element raster. Galileo NIMS bundles contain calibrated point-perspective spectral cubes.
proposals.work: Keep as research candidates. Reopen the specific recorded blockers only with new evidence.
proposals.limit: Registration, footprint geometry, calibration and coverage remain substantial work. Gaspra has a pre-existing calibration-source discrepancy; Ida's current false-color coverage is only 17.2% of the display mesh. These are not replacements for the broadly covered recommendations above.
proposals.checks: Compare the original label/calibration disagreement for Gaspra and the sparse source geometry for Ida. Do not treat a PDS4 migration as new calibration evidence. A negative result updates the existing ledger, not an invented map.

proposals.title: Eros: qualify derived gravity and physical parameters
proposals.current: Eros already has an observed shape and elevation. No new gravity map has been qualified by this audit.
proposals.result: Read the derived NEAR radio-science products and determine which gravity or physical facts add information beyond the current package.
proposals.evidence: The PDS4 scan located the NEAR RSS derived bundle separately from raw tracking.
proposals.work: Identify model coefficients, covariance, reference frame and radius; compare selected mass and spin facts before deriving any field offline.
proposals.limit: Spatial resolving power and reference-density assumptions constrain interpretation. No hidden-structure claims or automatic geometry replacement.
proposals.checks: Reproduce published check values and uncertainty. If no distinct reliable surface field exists, limit the PR to demonstrated fact corrections and the source decision.

proposals.title: Preserve quantitative map precision and source support
proposals.current: Bennu and Eros bands are shipped; several SPC moon packages already use albedo and radius products. Their auxiliary rasters are not all selected.
proposals.result: Improve numeric decoding, masks and source-support evidence where the native products expose more precision, counts, uncertainty, XYZ or observing angles.
proposals.evidence: The USGS audit identified Bennu ancillary products and a catalogue-versus-file dimension discrepancy; PDS4 supplies related SPC support products.
proposals.work: Compare exact current inputs to the native release, retain quantitative data through preparation, and use counts/angles to qualify measurements. Add a displayed quality view only if it answers a clear question within existing controls.
proposals.limit: Quality counts and uncertainty are not new physical quantities. Do not re-add existing bands, replace geometry, or create a Dataset details panel.
proposals.checks: Source samples, validity masks, precision loss, orientation and declared dimensions; an evidence-only result is valid if existing output is already adequate.

proposals.title: Mercury: qualify regional stereo maps
proposals.current: Native global BDR, LOI, enhanced color and numeric elevation are already shipped.
proposals.result: Add only regional stereo height or orthophoto products that demonstrably improve a useful close-up on the current body.
proposals.evidence: The USGS audit found 192 TIFF files in the Fassett release, including paired DEMs and orthophotos, plus a separate volatile-loss terrain product. PIA17385 identifies a north-polar MLA elevation lead; its datum and value over the selected global DEM need checking.
proposals.work: Pair DEMs and orthophotos, read frames and vertical datums, and compare the MLA polar grid and local volatile-loss DTM with current elevation. Rank measured footprint and detail gain before preparing a bounded subset.
proposals.limit: Regional coverage, fixed geometry and no duplicate global basemap rows. Keep output sampling separate from stereo accuracy.
proposals.checks: Independent elevations, overlap residuals, regional boundary masks and matched camera comparisons against the current global maps.

proposals.title: Moon: qualify regional terrain and photometric products
proposals.current: The Moon already has global imagery, elevation, thermal, mineral and geology views.
proposals.result: Prepare only local products whose numeric terrain or photometric information adds a measured improvement over those views.
proposals.evidence: The linked regional collection lists 15 TIFFs. Separate USGS records identify the Apollo 17 orthomosaic, south-polar DEM/slope and Haworth photoclinometry. PIA00090 adds an Aristarchus multispectral lead. Each remains a regional product with its own method and quality limits.
proposals.work: Match source quantity, map projection, scale, footprint and quality for each location. Group related variants through existing controls if a regional addition is warranted.
proposals.limit: Keep the mesh fixed. No global fill, duplicate mineral claims or separate photographs panel.
proposals.checks: Source-to-output values, regional bounds, landmark registration and visible benefit at the selected texture size.

proposals.title: Io: resolve the limits of the Tvashtar stereo product
proposals.current: The existing Io package does not have a qualified global height field from this source.
proposals.result: Determine whether the regional product supports any defensible relative-height display, and record the result in Io's investigation ledger.
proposals.evidence: The source explicitly calls the DEM uncontrolled, with an arbitrary elevation zero and possible long-baseline tilt.
proposals.work: Inspect the stereo solution, vertical reference and external control. Quantify residual tilt and local uncertainty before preparing any relative-height view.
proposals.limit: No absolute elevation, no global elevation layer and no geometry changes. Without new independent control this remains excluded from delivery.
proposals.checks: A reproducible control comparison and an explicit acceptance or rejection; visual plausibility is not sufficient.

proposals.title: Mercury: magnesium and other elemental measurements
proposals.current: Current Mercury adds MDIS imaging, numeric height and a MASCS spectrum; XRS/GRS surface chemistry is distinct from those.
proposals.result: Add qualified elemental ratios and neutron-absorption data from MESSENGER as one related measurement group.
proposals.evidence: PIA19242 shows Mg/Si and thermal-neutron absorption derived from XRS and GRS. It is an explanatory two-panel image, not the native numeric release.
proposals.work: Locate the underlying published grids and uncertainties through the source references, establish the effective footprint and longitude convention, then prepare numeric fields offline.
proposals.limit: Do not decode quantitative values from the press color palette or call a neutron-absorption signal a specific mineral abundance. Native release access and coverage are not yet verified.
proposals.checks: Check native units, scale, mask, uncertainty and published sample values. Release only if useful coverage and original numeric data are established.

proposals.title: Vesta: qualify VIR mineral and rock signatures
proposals.current: Vesta has FC spectral ratios. Its ledger already excludes the small NASA VIR press mineral map as a quantitative input.
proposals.result: Find and qualify the original VIR measurements or derived grids behind the mineral, hydration and rock-unit maps.
proposals.evidence: The supplied pages show distinct VIR interpretations, including pyroxene and hydration; they do not resolve the existing native-data blocker.
proposals.work: Trace products to calibrated VIR spectra and documented models, retain footprint and uncertainty, and convert their frame to the selected Claudia convention.
proposals.limit: Keep the existing exclusion unless reusable numeric or registered source products are found. Howardite, eucrite and diogenite are rock categories; a press color is not a mineral percentage.
proposals.checks: An original-product receipt, independent spectral samples, frame validation and a quantity-specific interpretation. Do not release an RGB-to-abundance reconstruction.

proposals.title: Vesta: mapped geological units
proposals.current: The selected Vesta views include photographs, spectral ratios and elevation, without this geological-unit map.
proposals.result: Qualify published geological units and original bright/dark deposit catalogues for Vesta through existing categorical and feature content.
proposals.evidence: PIA18788 combines 15 quadrangle maps in a Mollweide map using Dawn Claudia coordinates.
proposals.work: Locate original unit boundaries, deposit tables and legends. Keep mapped geological interpretation distinct from reflectance and the VIR mineral measurements in proposal 31.
proposals.limit: The press sheet includes labels and a legend; it is not a clean numeric input. Map units are interpreted terrain categories, not exact ages or measured mineral fractions.
proposals.checks: Verify unit boundaries, categorical resampling, landmark orientation, legend completeness and source reuse terms.

proposals.title: Titan: observed infrared surface coverage
proposals.current: Titan has current ISS, radar, terrain and geology. The ledger leaves the 2019 VIMS/ISS composite unresolved because filled pixels lack a validity mask.
proposals.result: Qualify a VIMS surface product that distinguishes observed spectral coverage from filled or seam-repaired areas.
proposals.evidence: The surface Photojournal pages discuss atmospheric/photometric correction and mosaics from many flybys. Their native masks remain essential. The separate atmospheric HCN observation is assigned to proposal 80.
proposals.work: Locate masks and native band or ratio products, identify footprints and source epochs, and document haze correction before selecting data.
proposals.limit: The new list does not remove the existing mask blocker. Apparent surface brightening is not proof of cryovolcanism. No synthetic global fill or atmospheric volume work.
proposals.checks: Measured coverage per band, common mask, calibration/photometry comparison, existing-ledger reopen evidence and fixed-scene registration.

proposals.title: Titan: measured seasonal temperature by latitude
proposals.current: Titan's selected views do not include this seasonal surface-temperature series.
proposals.result: Present Cassini CIRS seasonal temperatures as explicitly latitude-averaged observations, using the existing date selector or chart contract.
proposals.evidence: The source describes 19 µm measurements at two-year intervals from 2004 to 2016, averaged over longitude. Black regions have no data.
proposals.work: Find the numeric latitude/time measurements and uncertainty, preserve averaging windows and missing latitudes, then select a compact sequence.
proposals.limit: This is not a longitude-resolved surface temperature map. A zonal mean can only be displayed as such; the date is an averaging interval, not an instantaneous global observation.
proposals.checks: Reproduce latitude profiles from native data, retain uncertainty and check date labels and missing regions. If only the animation is available, stop before integration.

proposals.title: Ganymede: infrared ice and grain-size signatures
proposals.current: Ganymede has imaging, geology and an oxygen-signature view. A new NIMS product needs comparison with the existing deferred SPHERE/JWST composition work.
proposals.result: Qualify Galileo NIMS ice-sensitive bands or published grain-size interpretations as measured regional data.
proposals.evidence: PIA00500 compares camera imagery with NIMS water-ice and grain/mineral interpretations, but supplies a montage rather than a native scalar grid.
proposals.work: Identify the original observation cube, geometry, wavelengths, masks and interpretation method; measure useful coverage on the current body.
proposals.limit: Ice absorption, grain size and abundance are different quantities. Do not assign minerals from press colors or imply global coverage.
proposals.checks: Native cube samples, footprint/landmark registration, spectral uncertainty and explicit distinction from the oxygen dataset.

proposals.title: Ganymede: Galileo brightness temperatures
proposals.current: No corresponding measured PPR temperature map is selected.
proposals.result: A dated brightness-temperature view for the observed part of Ganymede, with the PPR footprint retained.
proposals.evidence: PIA01232 describes a 90–160 K daytime product. Its narrative contains inconsistent encounter/orbit wording, so native records must resolve the observation identity.
proposals.work: Recover the PPR numeric measurements and geometry, establish the epoch and radiometric interpretation, and prepare only the measured footprint.
proposals.limit: Brightness temperature is inferred from radiation and depends on assumptions; one sunlit encounter is not a global climate. No palette inversion.
proposals.checks: Resolve observation identity against native labels, independently check temperature samples and quantify footprint and uncertainty.

proposals.title: Phoebe, Iapetus and Enceladus: measured heat radiation
proposals.current: Reflectivity and infrared/ice data already exist on these moons. This proposal concerns CIRS heat measurements, separate from Enceladus VIMS work in the other chat.
proposals.result: Prepare selected dated CIRS temperature products and local-time comparisons, with one coherent source-qualified outcome per moon.
proposals.evidence: The supplied pages show Phoebe flyby temperatures, Iapetus dark-side temperatures and Enceladus south-polar heat. They include unobserved areas, model comparisons and different spatial footprints.
proposals.work: Obtain original CIRS measurements, footprints and uncertainties. Separate observed heat from predicted solar temperatures; choose only observations with useful coverage.
proposals.limit: Different local times cannot be merged into a simultaneous global map. The Iapetus curve is not a spatial raster. Do not animate geysers or modify geometry.
proposals.checks: Numeric temperature/brightness checks, explicit local time, measurement/model distinction, footprint masks and current-source overlap. Split implementation by moon if independent qualification outcomes differ.

proposals.title: Enceladus: published geyser source locations
proposals.current: Existing named features do not establish this research catalogue. Enceladus VIMS imagery is already being worked on elsewhere.
proposals.result: Add the published jet-source catalogue through the existing feature contract, retaining uncertainty and research identifiers.
proposals.evidence: The source page describes 100 plotted geyser sources, circles showing position uncertainty, and additional qualifications for poorly constrained tilts or single-image detections. It points to the 2014 papers.
proposals.work: Acquire the original coordinate table, resolve source counts/definitions and projection, and compare with existing IAU features. Record uncertainty even if the current feature UI cannot draw error circles.
proposals.limit: Locations are not a current activity forecast, animated plume or IAU naming catalogue. No new feature panel or invented jet geometry.
proposals.checks: Match published IDs and coordinates, verify south-polar registration and account for ambiguous detections without merging them silently.

proposals.title: Ceres: catalogue of bright deposits
proposals.current: Ceres has named features and composition maps; the more-than-300 bright-area classification has not been joined to those features.
proposals.result: Add source-backed deposit locations and their geological setting through existing feature content.
proposals.evidence: The NASA page groups bright areas by crater floor, rim/wall, ejecta and Ahuna Mons setting.
proposals.work: Retrieve the research table behind the plot, match coordinates and IDs, and preserve category definitions and survey completeness.
proposals.limit: Do not infer chemical composition from brightness alone or digitize plotted dots as exact coordinates. Avoid duplicating existing named faculae.
proposals.checks: Row count, deduplication, coordinate frame, cross-match to named features and uncertainty. Release only with a reusable source catalogue.

proposals.title: Pluto: geological units around Sputnik Planitia
proposals.current: Pluto already has imagery, height and three fitted ice fractions; geological terrain units are a different interpreted dataset.
proposals.result: Prepare the published regional geological mapping with a categorical legend and an honest footprint.
proposals.evidence: The two supplied pages are versions of the same geological map and legend, covering Sputnik Planitia and surrounding terrain rather than the full globe.
proposals.work: Locate original polygons or a registered categorical release, preserve unit codes and source-map scale, and use the current categorical preparation lane.
proposals.limit: Do not create two datasets from the map and its legend. Units describe mapped morphology; they are not measured ages or direct ice fractions.
proposals.checks: Native boundary checks, source frame, categorical resampling, legend parity and missing-area visibility.

proposals.title: Io: dated volcanic changes and thermal observations
proposals.current: Io already has a JIRAM volcanic-heat view from orbits 41, 43, 47 and 49, with 22% measured coverage. The current hotspot table serves as validation, not a second live lens.
proposals.result: Add qualified dated observations of surface change or heat that are distinct from the existing JIRAM map.
proposals.evidence: PIA26526 identifies JunoCam observations from April, October and December 2024 with different resolutions. Older Galileo pages show PPR temperatures and observed surface changes.
proposals.work: Recover native JunoCam/SSI/PPR observations, keep epochs and instrument quantities separate, and compare registered common footprints. Assess later JIRAM observations under the current ledger. Treat the 242-volcano historical reconstruction and heat-flow model as separate interpreted products requiring their original numeric data; do not revive the retired point-symbol lens.
proposals.limit: Different brightness processing is not proof of change. PPR temperature and JIRAM radiance are not interchangeable. The PPR night map warns that some edge temperatures may be spurious.
proposals.checks: Matched registration and resolution, common-footprint masks, native radiometry and source-time labels. Do not replace measured heat with a modeled prediction from PIA16941.

proposals.title: Jupiter: dated visible and infrared observations
proposals.current: Jupiter already has dated OPAL visible maps plus UV and methane views. More OPAL dates already present are not new work.
proposals.result: Add a small number of scientifically distinct historical observing sets, with regional NIMS/PPR products considered only if the original geometry and quantity are recoverable.
proposals.evidence: The individual entries span Voyager, Galileo, Cassini, New Horizons, Juno and ground-based observing sets. They include cylindrical maps, spectral/time sequences, pressure-sensitive infrared measurements and regional impact observations. One PR should release a coherent qualified set rather than combine unrelated epochs.
proposals.work: Group by actual observation and wavelength, recover native map boundaries and longitude system, and select coherent epochs. Use existing date/band arrows.
proposals.limit: A historical partial hemisphere cannot silently fill a modern OPAL map. A PPR pressure-level temperature is not a solid-surface temperature. No artificial animation from unrelated exposures.
proposals.checks: Resolve each epoch and observing interval, validate longitude systems and common footprints, and compare source-calibrated channels without independent cosmetic stretches.

proposals.title: Saturn: coherent historical observing sets
proposals.current: Saturn already has dated OPAL, UV and methane maps. Its ledger rejects a Cassini polar cap pasted into the 2025 OPAL body.
proposals.result: Qualify one coherent Voyager or Cassini visible/infrared set as a separately dated dataset if coverage supports the existing map contract.
proposals.evidence: The individual review includes Voyager observations, Cassini visible/infrared narrow-strip mosaics and southern-hemisphere UV imagery.
proposals.work: Find original map-projected products, observing intervals, ring/limb masks and longitude conventions. Measure coverage before committing to a surface view.
proposals.limit: This does not reopen cross-mission cap filling or claim the narrow-strip images are ready global maps. No cloud geometry or renderer work.
proposals.checks: Native observation identity, geometry, bandpass, measured footprint and actual improvement over the existing historical set.

proposals.title: Saturn rings: qualify radial spectral measurements
proposals.current: Ring opacity uses a measured UVIS profile, but radius-indexed color is unresolved. Perspective Photojournal images do not meet that requirement.
proposals.result: Find a calibrated radius-indexed VIMS spectral profile that can be prepared within the existing ring contract, or record why it cannot.
proposals.evidence: PIA23170 shows spectral variation across A, B and C rings. Its colors mix ice purity and grain-size effects and are not a ready radial measurement file.
proposals.work: Trace the native VIMS scan and geometry, preserve radial resolution and quality flags, then check whether current prepared ring assets can represent the qualified quantity.
proposals.limit: No renderer or ring-topology changes. If the existing contract cannot support the result, keep an evidence-only PR. Do not infer grain size or abundance from press RGB values.
proposals.checks: Published radial calibration and uncertainty, scan-to-radius mapping, current-contract feasibility and no regression in the selected opacity profile.

proposals.title: Tempel 1: qualify a body package and thermal observation
proposals.current: No Tempel 1 package appears in the pinned source snapshot. The PSI PDS4 tree does not include the full separate UMD comet archive.
proposals.result: A source-intake proposal for a genuine observed comet package, followed by a dated thermal view only if its shape, camera and data can be qualified through the generic object contract.
proposals.evidence: The Photojournal thermal page describes a modeled separation of reflected and emitted light from Deep Impact infrared observations; the imagery is regional on the nucleus.
proposals.work: Locate the original UMD/PDS comet products, shape, frame, images and thermal interpretation. Establish acquisition and registration before promising a new rendered object.
proposals.limit: The current audit has not downloaded or qualified those holdings. Do not create a fallback scene from the press montage. No renderer redesign or synthetic whole-nucleus temperature.
