proposals.checks: A complete original-source intake, generic-adapter compatibility, camera/shape evidence, uncertainty and measured coverage before any package release.

proposals.title: Moon: GRAIL gravity anomalies
proposals.current: The Moon already has crustal thickness and topography; a gravitational anomaly is a distinct modeled quantity.
proposals.result: Add a qualified GRAIL Bouguer anomaly map and retain local Orientale/dike illustrations as supporting leads only.
proposals.evidence: PIA16623 describes gravity after removal of topographic attraction. The supplied movie is not the original coefficient or grid release.
proposals.work: Obtain published coefficients or numeric grids and model assumptions, evaluate them offline if needed, and record degree, density and reference-radius choices.
proposals.limit: An anomaly does not uniquely identify a buried rock type or cavity. Keep the existing crustal-thickness product distinct and the mesh unchanged.
proposals.checks: Independent published check values, model truncation, units, orientation and uncertainty; avoid interpreting grid spacing as resolving power.

proposals.title: Moon and Mercury: observed polar illumination
proposals.current: Current temperature and elevation views do not themselves show an observed illumination-frequency survey.
proposals.result: Prepare published polar illumination fractions with explicit observation windows and polar footprints.
proposals.evidence: The lunar page describes a six-month WAC stack over 88°S–90°S. The Mercury page is a separate polar-illumination source lead and needs its own method check.
proposals.work: Locate original fractional rasters, observation counts and coverage, keeping observed time sampling separate from a long-term lighting simulation.
proposals.limit: Six months of images do not prove permanent darkness or annual sunlight percentage. This is a prepared data view, not changes to runtime sunlight or shadows.
proposals.checks: Native fractions and denominator, exact time window, polar projection, missing cells and independent source-map comparison.

proposals.title: Earth: measured soil moisture and freeze/thaw
proposals.current: Earth has imagery, terrain, night lights and a temperature-anomaly view. SMAP moisture and freeze/thaw are distinct proposed quantities.
proposals.result: Add one compact SMAP soil-moisture observation set; include freeze/thaw only from its own valid product and categorical definition.
proposals.evidence: The supplied pages include commissioning-era radiometer/radar products and later surface-moisture maps. They have different spatial resolutions and gaps.
proposals.work: Select a versioned numeric product, retain acquisition interval, quality flags, land/ice mask and uncertainty, and prepare a bounded date set offline.
proposals.limit: Do not confuse brightness temperature with soil moisture or commissioning maps with uninterrupted operational coverage. Original-data access has not been verified by this Photojournal audit.
proposals.checks: Official-unit samples, invalid-value handling, measured footprint, date averaging and incremental source value over existing Earth layers.

proposals.title: Earth: ocean salinity and sea-level anomalies
proposals.current: The selected Earth ocean views include bathymetry and a temperature anomaly, not these two quantities.
proposals.result: Prepare versioned salinity and sea-surface-height anomalies as separate measured quantities under existing dataset/date controls.
proposals.evidence: Aquarius and Jason Photojournal pages identify the source instruments and dated examples. Those rendered images are leads to the original gridded measurements.
proposals.work: Retrieve documented numeric products with land/coast masks, averaging windows, uncertainty and reference climatology. Select a small matched set of intervals rather than an unbounded time archive.
proposals.limit: Salinity, sea level and ocean temperature cannot share units or a common quantitative scale. Sea-level anomaly is relative to a stated reference, not ocean depth.
proposals.checks: Native values, units, anomaly reference, coastal masking, temporal coverage and separate color scales.

proposals.title: Earth: monthly gravity changes from GRACE
proposals.current: The existing Earth package does not establish this monthly gravity-anomaly series.
proposals.result: A compact source-qualified set of GRACE gravity changes, or an explicitly interpreted mass-equivalent product if that is the selected release.
proposals.evidence: PIA22448 describes near-monthly gravity-anomaly maps from April 2002 to June 2017; it does not provide the full numeric interpretation contract.
proposals.work: Identify a versioned official solution, its reference interval, corrections, masks and uncertainties. Prepare a declared sequence through the existing date selector.
proposals.limit: Do not interchange gravity anomaly and water-equivalent thickness. Spatial smoothing and missing months matter; the press animation alone is insufficient.
proposals.checks: Independent monthly samples, reference mean, leakage/smoothing treatment, unit labels and no interpolation disguised as observations.

proposals.title: Earth: thermal emissivity and mapped surface minerals
proposals.current: Earth's photographic basemap does not measure infrared emission efficiency or EMIT mineral signatures.
proposals.result: Add separate ASTER emissivity and EMIT mineral data groups if their native coverage and quality masks support useful prepared views.
proposals.evidence: ASTER provides an emissivity lead; EMIT's map concerns arid regions and named mineral signatures, not an everywhere-complete global composition map.
proposals.work: Acquire versioned bands and numeric mineral products, preserve wavelength, quality and footprint, and explain unfamiliar mineral names in ordinary language.
proposals.limit: Emissivity is not temperature. Mineral presence, spectral fit and abundance are different products. Do not treat unsurveyed areas as zero or use the press RGB mixture as numeric concentrations.
proposals.checks: Band units and scaling, independent samples, land/validity masks, declared effective resolution and a measured-coverage report for each product family.

proposals.title: Earth: atmospheric gases and microwave observations
proposals.current: Existing Earth imagery and clouds do not establish measured CO₂, CO, dust, methane-plume or microwave fields.
proposals.result: Qualify a small set of atmosphere measurements that can be described faithfully on an existing map or chart, without adding atmospheric rendering.
proposals.evidence: The supplied pages include mid-tropospheric AIRS gases, regional methane plumes and 34 GHz COWVR emissions. They sample different altitudes and quantities.
proposals.work: Choose original numeric products and record pressure/altitude sensitivity, time interval, retrieval quality and footprint. Keep local plume detections separate from global fields.
proposals.limit: These are not surface chemistry maps. Microwave brightness is not a direct wind or humidity measurement without the retrieval. Emission-rate estimates need their wind/model uncertainty.
proposals.checks: Source quantity and vertical sensitivity, native samples, masks and epoch. Stop if the existing content contract cannot clearly preserve these distinctions.

proposals.title: Earth: measured ice motion
proposals.current: Earth has static terrain and imagery. Measured ice flow and regional cryosphere products require separate source qualification.
proposals.result: Prepare a measured Antarctic ice-speed field, with separate qualification of Iceland ice motion and source snow-water products.
proposals.evidence: The Antarctic page identifies a radar-interferometry velocity map with 300 m sampling. Other supplied pages concern local ice speed, snow and coastal bathymetry.
proposals.work: Retrieve original grids, observation dates and uncertainties. Use a scalar speed view if supported; retain direction in the data without inventing motion arrows or animation.
proposals.limit: Sampling is not accuracy and an old survey is not current ice motion. Snow water content is a different quantity from speed. Coastal Greenland bathymetry belongs in proposal 66.
proposals.checks: Velocity components and units, speed calculation, polar projection, missing areas, epoch and comparison with the source map.

proposals.title: Earth: qualify regional change and hazard maps
proposals.current: The Earth package has global views; the supplied ARIA, ASTER, ECOSTRESS and radar examples are mostly local events.
proposals.result: A bounded intake PR identifying a small set of scientifically clear regional measurements, such as ground displacement, flood extent or surface temperature, that fit the existing map contract.
proposals.evidence: The Photojournal list contains many earthquake, flood, fire and deformation maps. They are separate products with different observation windows and uncertainty.
proposals.work: Group by physical quantity, recover original georeferenced data and quality flags, and choose one representative source-qualified event per supported quantity before expanding.
proposals.limit: A damage-proxy signal is not a building-damage survey. Thermal burn-risk examples are not a forecast. Do not revive an unrelated local-imagery or surface-photographs UI.
proposals.checks: Before/after time alignment, units, projection, uncertainty, valid footprint and whether current zoom/detail can display the result usefully. Retain low-value cases in the ledger instead of adding clutter.

proposals.title: Europa: measure the value of controlled regional mosaics
proposals.current: Europa already uses a broad set of individual CLEAR images, plus global and other mission imagery.
proposals.result: Replace or extend existing photography only where the controlled mosaic release improves registration, measured coverage or useful close-up detail.
proposals.evidence: The USGS audit identifies a 92-mosaic archive overlapping the current 332 individual CLEAR images. The press close-ups are supporting observation leads, not 92 new datasets.
proposals.work: Cross-match observation IDs and map versions, measure geometric and coverage differences, and select replacements only after a matched preparation comparison.
proposals.limit: Keep geometry and current photographic controls. No separate photo gallery, global gap filling or claim that a newer wrapper improves resolution.
proposals.checks: Image-source deduplication, common-landmark residuals, measured area and delivered bytes at the same camera and texture budget.

proposals.title: Pluto, Ceres and Vesta: qualify historical telescope maps
proposals.current: Spacecraft maps already provide better spatial detail. Historical telescope observations would only add a supported epoch or wavelength comparison.
proposals.result: Determine whether one historical observing set supports a useful dated map or whole-object observation within current controls.
proposals.evidence: Photojournal contains Hubble maps of Pluto and Vesta; PDS4 contains historical HST Ceres products. Different inversions and resolutions prevent a direct pixel-by-pixel change claim.
proposals.work: Recover original products and reconstruction assumptions, compare on common support/resolution, and preserve observation dates separately from publication dates.
proposals.limit: Do not sharpen old telescope maps with later spacecraft detail or infer surface change from different image-processing methods. No automatic replacement of current global maps.
proposals.checks: Original product and method availability, effective resolution, geometry and calibration consistency. Keep an evidence-only result if a faithful comparison cannot be made.

proposals.title: Ganymede: controlled close-up photography
proposals.current: Global monochrome, enhanced color, geology and oxygen data already exist. New photographs must improve measured coverage, registration or useful detail.
proposals.result: Qualify a small set of native Galileo SSI regional mosaics, starting with Uruk Sulcus and Galileo Regio.
proposals.evidence: The individual review found roughly 74 m and 80 m sampling in close-up products, plus mixed-resolution color composites. These are regional observations.
proposals.work: Recover original calibrated frames and control geometry; cross-match frame IDs against the current photography; compare native and prepared detail at identical viewing conditions.
proposals.limit: The press insets and color composites are not georeferenced scalar products. Do not manufacture high-resolution color by treating a coarse color overlay as fine measured detail.
proposals.checks: Landmark residuals, source frame identities, valid footprint, actual resolution and delivered bytes. Add only a demonstrated improvement on the fixed body.

proposals.title: Callisto: controlled close-up photography
proposals.current: Callisto already has global photography, Galileo color and infrared observations.
proposals.result: Qualify additional SSI coverage around Valhalla, Asgard and the southern hemisphere where it adds useful observed detail.
proposals.evidence: The reviewed pages distinguish fine pixel sampling from coarser resolved features; PIA00561's sampling does not mean every 46 m feature is resolved. Other products combine coarse color with finer monochrome.
proposals.work: Obtain the native images and observation geometry, measure overlap with selected inputs, and prepare only controlled regional footprints.
proposals.limit: No global gap filling or claim that every press crop is a separate dataset. Infrared measurements belong in proposal 12.
proposals.checks: Independent image registration, resolution comparison, illumination differences, masks and byte budget.

proposals.title: Neptune: a dated Voyager cloud observation
proposals.current: Neptune uses OPAL maps and a qualified color reference. Its ledger already defers older OPAL maps with a different photometric coefficient.
proposals.result: Determine whether a separate Voyager epoch adds a faithful historical cloud observation through the current dataset controls.
proposals.evidence: PIA00050 shows a partial southern-hemisphere observation, not a complete timeless surface map.
proposals.work: Recover original Voyager filters, timing and camera geometry; determine the required prepared photometric treatment and measured coverage.
proposals.limit: No renderer change, no insertion into modern OPAL gaps and no inference of cloud evolution from unmatched processing. A dated dataset is conditional on current-contract compatibility.
proposals.checks: Source identity, longitude convention, calibrated band combination, footprint and the existing photometry ledger's constraints.

proposals.title: Earth and Moon: historical Galileo spectral observations
proposals.current: Modern global maps already supply better basemap detail. Galileo offers a different observing epoch or wavelength, not an automatic replacement.
proposals.result: Qualify a compact set of dated Galileo Earth/Moon bands where the scientific difference is useful.
proposals.evidence: The supplied entries include an Antarctic limb mosaic, green and near-infrared lunar imagery, Andes observations and a 24-hour Earth mosaic. Their geometry and time support differ.
proposals.work: Group exposures by actual encounter and band; retrieve native calibrated values, poses and footprints; preserve observation intervals.
proposals.limit: A 24-hour mosaic is not simultaneous Earth illumination. Never wrap an unregistered camera image onto the whole globe or introduce a photograph gallery.
proposals.checks: Registration, band response, dates, view geometry and common support for any comparison.

proposals.title: Venus: qualify regional Magellan radar detail
proposals.current: Venus already has global radar, height, emissivity, reflectivity and roughness products.
proposals.result: Use finer native radar mosaics only where they improve useful regional detail at the existing asset budget.
proposals.evidence: PIA00086 identifies a Lavinia Planitia F-MIDR region; PIA00461 supplies a separate Bahet/Onatah lead.
proposals.work: Locate original F-MIDR products, preserve radar geometry and calibration, and run a matched comparison against the selected global radar map.
proposals.limit: Radar brightness is not optical color. Pixel sampling is not terrain resolution, and a small regional patch does not solve poor global coverage.
proposals.checks: Native footprint and calibration, look-direction differences, source/prepared comparison and improvement per byte.

proposals.title: Earth: calibrated radar mosaics and land measurements
proposals.current: Earth's optical basemap does not show calibrated radar backscatter or radar-derived biomass.
proposals.result: Qualify a broad radar mosaic first, with land-cover or biomass products treated as separate measured or modeled quantities.
proposals.evidence: The reviewed set includes the JERS-1 equatorial Africa mosaic, Raco land cover and biomass, Arctic RADARSAT and regional oil/lava examples.
proposals.work: Obtain calibrated georeferenced bands, incidence-angle information and masks. Distinguish native radar measurements from classifications and retrievals.
proposals.limit: Proposal 54 owns individual event comparisons; this proposal owns calibrated radar source handling and a representative broad mosaic. Do not publish a biomass model as raw radar reflectivity.
proposals.checks: Units, polarization, acquisition interval, incidence correction, independent numeric samples and declared footprint.

proposals.title: Eros: qualify low-altitude MSI close-ups
proposals.current: Seven MSI bands and global photography are already selected. The repository also has preparation evidence for registered native MSI images.
proposals.result: Add a bounded regional improvement from native close-flyby images if it survives a same-budget comparison.
proposals.evidence: The Photojournal sequence includes low-altitude observations and mosaics of boulders, craters and smooth deposits. A rendered drape is not an original MSI frame.
proposals.work: Cross-match source image IDs, retrieve calibrated frames and qualified backplanes, then measure new detail and support on the existing shape.
proposals.limit: Do not re-add the seven global bands. Pond coordinates belong in proposal 07; speculative boulder-size measurements from a press image are excluded.
proposals.checks: Existing camera-oracle compatibility, independent landmarks, source sampling, valid mask and prepared byte cost.

proposals.title: Jupiter rings: qualify a measured radial profile
proposals.current: A perspective ring photograph does not establish a radius-indexed measurement suitable for the current prepared ring contract.
proposals.result: Determine whether Galileo observations support a calibrated radial brightness profile usable by the existing ring preparation.
proposals.evidence: PIA03001 identifies a backlit Galileo ring mosaic and its observing geometry.
proposals.work: Recover the original images and geometry, distinguish forward-scattering brightness from optical depth, and assess the current ring asset contract before deriving a profile offline.
proposals.limit: No renderer or ring-topology changes. A photograph alone cannot establish a three-dimensional dust distribution or opacity law.
proposals.checks: Radius mapping, scattering angle, background subtraction, uncertainty and current-contract feasibility; otherwise record a bounded negative result.

proposals.title: Mercury: historical and additional spectral observations
proposals.current: Native global BDR, LOI, enhanced color, elevation and a MASCS spectrum are already selected.
proposals.result: Qualify a distinct Mariner 10 epoch or measured MDIS filter set beyond the existing enhanced-color view.
proposals.evidence: The reviewed entries include Mariner 10 maps and a MESSENGER sequence of five scenes in eleven filters. Press RGB maps do not retain all those measurements.
proposals.work: Identify original filters, calibration, epochs and registered footprints; compare their actual values and coverage with current inputs.
proposals.limit: No duplicate row for a press rendering of the shipped global map. Keep measured bands distinct from an enhanced-color composite and from elemental products in proposal 30.
proposals.checks: Band centers, scale, geometry, common footprint and an explicit statement of what the addition teaches.

proposals.title: Earth: regional elevation and bathymetry improvements
proposals.current: Earth already uses GEBCO 2026 for global terrain and bathymetry.
proposals.result: Replace or supplement regional numeric height data only where SRTM, AIRSAR or ocean surveys demonstrably improve it.
proposals.evidence: The supplied entries include California and Eurasian SRTM, Umnak AIRSAR and OMG coastal Greenland bathymetry.
proposals.work: Recover original numeric grids and vertical datums; compare measured detail, gaps and uncertainty against the exact GEBCO samples.
proposals.limit: No mesh change, height inferred from shaded relief or extra row for a coarser historical map. Coastal bathymetry is distinct from ice-flow velocity.
proposals.checks: Independent elevations/depths, vertical datum, shoreline, masks, source resolution and visible improvement within existing zoom and byte budgets.

proposals.title: Earth: spectral mosaics and vegetation observations
proposals.current: Blue Marble photography does not preserve ASTER or AVIRIS spectral bands or measured vegetation stress.
proposals.result: Qualify one useful native spectral observing set, with separately defined vegetation products when their source retrieval is available.
proposals.evidence: The reviewed pages identify Anti-Atlas ASTER, North American MISR, Rim Fire AVIRIS, Sierra forest stress and SHIFT flight coverage. The ASTER global browse mosaic was assembled from thumbnails.
proposals.work: Verify public product availability, acquire calibrated bands and geometry, retain acquisition dates and quality flags, and compare source support with current imagery.
proposals.limit: The SHIFT flight map is an availability lead, not proof the native cube is downloadable. A thumbnail mosaic or added shaded relief is not calibrated surface reflectance.
proposals.checks: Native access, band wavelengths/units, registration, measured footprint and uncertainty for any derived vegetation quantity.

proposals.title: Saturn moons: controlled ISS regional photography
proposals.current: These moons already have global photography. Enceladus VIMS composition work belongs to the other active proposal, not this one.
proposals.result: Qualify useful native ISS close-ups on the existing body geometry, starting with the strongest measurable detail gain.
proposals.evidence: The individual entries include Phoebe, Rhea, Dione, Tethys and Mimas regions and Enceladus close-flyby mosaics, including a 12.3 m sampling example.
proposals.work: For each moon, deduplicate against current source images, obtain controlled poses and calibrated frames, and record an independent go/no-go result before preparing an addition.
proposals.limit: Sampling is not uniform resolved detail. Regional imagery must retain its footprint and shadows. No new surface-photo panel or replacement geometry.
proposals.checks: Per-body current-input comparison, landmark residuals, footprint, effective detail and byte budget. Implement successful bodies separately when their source work is independent.

proposals.title: Titan: dated ISS and radar observations
proposals.current: Titan already uses the USGS 2026 ISS map, mission-end SAR, terrain and geology. Historical cumulative mosaics often add no independent coverage.
proposals.result: Qualify actual dated observations that support a useful regional or temporal comparison, including radar lake observations.
proposals.evidence: The supplied set spans 2004–2015 releases, individual flybys, cumulative maps and Sotra terrain. PIA19658 was published in 2015 but its source observations end in April 2014.
proposals.work: Resolve each exposure interval, recover native bands and SAR geometry, separate cumulative-map revisions from observations, and compare on common support.
proposals.limit: Atmospheric correction and changing look angle can mimic surface changes. VIMS spectra belong in proposal 33; mapped geological units belong in 70.
proposals.checks: Actual observing dates, instrument units, registration, masks and any change claim tested against processing and viewing differences.

proposals.title: Enceladus and Titan: published fracture and terrain maps
proposals.current: Titan already has a global geological map. Regional boundaries and Enceladus fracture traces need their own original coordinate source.
proposals.result: Qualify source-published Enceladus fracture traces and Titan local geological units through the existing feature or categorical-map contract.
proposals.evidence: The reviewed entries include Enceladus north/south fracture maps and interpreted Titan terrain near proposed volcanic features.
proposals.work: Locate original linework or registered categorical files, preserve map scale and unit definitions, and cross-match current named features and Titan geological units.
proposals.limit: A proposed volcanic interpretation is not a confirmed eruption. Do not digitize press annotations as exact surveyed coordinates or add plume geometry.
proposals.checks: Original coordinate access, frame, line/region topology, scale, legend and distinct value over current maps. Keep separate source decisions per body.

proposals.title: Titan: qualify Huygens descent imaging
proposals.current: Global Titan products do not resolve the Huygens landing region at descent-image scales.
proposals.result: Establish whether original DISR observations can be registered as a very small measured regional dataset on the existing body.
proposals.evidence: The supplied pages show mosaics taken from several altitudes, including river-like channels and a roughly 1.3 km landing-region footprint.
proposals.work: Recover calibrated DISR frames, descent poses and the relevant terrain reference. Verify the image-triplet accounting against native records rather than the press montage.
proposals.limit: No surface-photo panel and no panorama wrapped around the globe. The small footprint may have no useful presentation at current zoom limits.
proposals.checks: Authoritative camera/terrain registration, native pixel geometry, footprint and demonstrable value within existing controls; stop if those conditions fail.

proposals.title: HD 189733b: qualify a historical Spitzer thermal comparison
proposals.current: The package already includes a JWST/Spitzer eclipse map, uncertainties and spectra. Earlier Spitzer maps are explicitly excluded unless a deposited numeric map adds a worthwhile comparison.
proposals.result: Resolve that specific source-availability condition for the 2007 Spitzer observations; add a historical result only if it is scientifically distinct and faithfully comparable.
proposals.evidence: PIA09376 and PIA09377 describe a phase-curve inversion, not a resolved photograph. Rediscovering these illustrations does not satisfy the existing ledger.
proposals.work: Locate the original data and reconstruction, establish longitudinal and latitudinal support, and account for data reused in the current fit.
proposals.limit: No new body or invented temperature texture. Model dependence and systematics must remain explicit; a press illustration cannot reopen the exclusion by itself.
proposals.checks: Deposited numeric availability, independent reconstruction checks, shared-data dependence, uncertainty and explicit ledger reopen evidence.

proposals.title: Atlas: qualify additional observed ISS coverage
proposals.current: Atlas already uses calibrated 2017 ISS images. Its ledger records a failed 2026 trial where published camera geometry projected about 98% of illuminated pixels onto sky.
proposals.result: Assess the December 2015 anti-Saturn view only if its original frames and authoritative geometry add measured coverage beyond the current set.
proposals.evidence: PIA17206 identifies a resolved ridge observation. A press portrait does not itself repair the known pointing problem.
proposals.work: Cross-match observation IDs, obtain original calibrated pixels and independent controlled poses, and compare the footprint with the selected 2017 sources.
proposals.limit: No guessed pointing adjustment, synthetic far side or replacement shape. Respect the existing press-portrait exclusion until genuinely new pixels or registration are established.
proposals.checks: Original camera solution, independent landmark residuals, new measured area and fixed-geometry preparation.

proposals.title: Planck: qualified all-sky scientific maps
proposals.current: The audit has not established a compatible current all-sky prepared content path for these three quantities.
proposals.result: Qualify native CMB, lensing and polarized-dust data and identify a faithful existing image or catalogue presentation before any integration.
proposals.evidence: PIA16873, PIA16875 and PIA18048 concern temperature anisotropy, inferred lensing matter and polarized dust respectively.
proposals.work: Obtain official numeric HEALPix releases with units, masks, coordinates and uncertainty; reduce to supported prepared content offline only if the present contract permits it.
proposals.limit: A sky map is not a planet texture. Lensing is an inference, and dust polarization is not a three-dimensional magnetic field. No renderer or world-ownership changes.
proposals.checks: Official product identity, coordinate transformations, numeric samples, uncertainty and current-contract fit. If no fit exists, the PR is a source qualification record only.

proposals.title: NED and the stellar halo: qualify catalogue measurements
proposals.current: The audit has not yet joined these observations to the existing catalogue packages.
proposals.result: Identify a bounded set of genuinely missing catalogue facts or prepared statistical content backed by the original survey.
proposals.evidence: PIA21084 shows NED galaxy distribution; PIA24571 depicts an inferred outer Milky Way halo density structure. Their pictures are not ready three-dimensional scene assets.
proposals.work: Find original row identifiers, distance uncertainties and selection functions, cross-match current entries, and select only supported facts or existing-chart results.
proposals.limit: No unbounded catalogue import, false depth from image pixels or renderer/world redesign. Native product access and incremental value remain unverified.
proposals.checks: Stable IDs, coordinate/distance conventions, population selection, uncertainty and row-level before/after changes.

proposals.title: Nebulae: calibrated infrared image layers
proposals.current: The reviewed products have not been matched to an existing image-layer package or scientifically qualified by this audit.
proposals.result: Qualify measured infrared bands for the California Nebula and Cygnus X through an existing image-layer contract where supported.
proposals.evidence: PIA23650 shows Spitzer dust emission; PIA26748 identifies SPHEREx water-ice and carbon-bearing spectral signatures in Cygnus X.
proposals.work: Recover native calibrated images or cubes, WCS, band definitions, errors and masks; compare any existing target inputs before preparing additional layers.
proposals.limit: These are projected measurements. No invented depth, volumetric nebula reconstruction or renderer change. Spectral signatures are not automatically abundance maps.
proposals.checks: Native availability, WCS registration, units, common band footprint and independent sample comparisons.

proposals.title: 3I/ATLAS: measured infrared coma spectra
proposals.current: The audit has not qualified a current package or an original downloadable measurement set for this lead.
proposals.result: Present a source-qualified spectrum or dated image through existing content if the native measurements are available and compatible.
proposals.evidence: PIA26720 describes December 2025 SPHEREx observations of dust, water, carbon-bearing material and carbon dioxide in the coma.
proposals.work: Locate the released spectra/images, preserve aperture, observation dates, wavelengths, calibration and uncertainties, and verify a suitable existing content owner.
proposals.limit: A coma is not a nucleus surface. Do not paint these signatures onto an asteroid mesh or invent a new particle renderer.
proposals.checks: Native product availability, aperture/geometry, line identification versus model interpretation, uncertainty and existing-contract compatibility.

proposals.title: Earth: coastal water measurements and their interpretation
proposals.current: The existing Earth layers do not establish the Belize protected-area measurements behind this study.
proposals.result: Qualify measured turbidity and water-temperature inputs, with any published protected-area risk score clearly retained as a separate model interpretation.
proposals.evidence: PIA25862 describes a MODIS-based study involving 24 protected areas and a published risk ranking.
proposals.work: Obtain original measured fields, time windows, area boundaries and the ranking method. Preserve the distinction between direct observations and aggregated conclusions.
proposals.limit: The historical ranking is not a current forecast or direct satellite measurement. Do not color whole regions from a press diagram without its underlying data.
proposals.checks: Boundary joins, native units, temporal aggregation, uncertainty and reproducibility of any retained ranking.

proposals.title: Jupiter: gravity-constrained deep winds
proposals.current: Jupiter has cloud imagery and magnetic data; the audit has not established whether the published deep-wind constraints are already reflected in its factual content.
proposals.result: Add only missing, source-backed facts or an existing-chart representation of the inferred wind-depth model.
proposals.evidence: PIA26076 illustrates Juno gravity constraints on winds extending roughly 3,000 km deep. The illustration itself is not a numeric field.
proposals.work: Read the original model and uncertainties, locate reusable parameter/profile data and compare current interior facts before editing content.
proposals.limit: No new interior geometry or animated flow. Gravity constrains a model; it does not directly photograph cylindrical winds.
proposals.checks: Original inference and uncertainty, published profile reproduction, current-content comparison and no unsupported spatial precision.

proposals.title: Titan: the measured south-polar HCN signature
proposals.current: Titan surface VIMS, thermal and geological products do not represent an atmospheric HCN cloud spectrum.
proposals.result: Qualify the observed polar-vortex spectrum as a dated atmospheric measurement using existing chart or factual content.
proposals.evidence: PIA18431 identifies hydrogen-cyanide ice in Titan's south-polar atmospheric vortex, a different target and interpretation from surface reflectance.
proposals.work: Find the original VIMS observation, spectral extraction and reference comparison; retain altitude/limb geometry, date and uncertainty.
proposals.limit: No surface HCN-abundance map, cloud volume or renderer change. A detection spectrum is not a global atmospheric concentration measurement.
proposals.checks: Original band samples, feature identification, aperture/geometry, observational support and existing chart compatibility.

proposals.title: Ceres: measured topography inside polar craters
proposals.current: The current elevation view withholds polar caps because its source cannot separate stereo measurements from interpolation.
proposals.result: Assess the separate nine-crater SPC release for genuinely measured regional height/albedo support within those withheld areas.
proposals.evidence: The PDS4 bundle describes secondary-illumination reconstruction inside permanently shadowed regions and a v2 correction to regional albedo orientations.
proposals.work: Inspect each crater's native grid, reconstruction quality, frame and validity. Transfer qualified scalar height/albedo onto the existing Ceres geometry; leave all unsupported surrounding areas missing.
proposals.limit: This is not permission to fill the entire polar caps or replace the displayed mesh. A new source must satisfy the existing measurement-versus-interpolation blocker.
proposals.checks: Per-crater native samples, corrected orientation, error/validity records, independent registration and explicit ledger reopen evidence.

proposals.title: Itokawa: calibrated near-infrared spectra
proposals.current: AMICA photographic bands do not supply the NIRS spectral measurements.
proposals.result: Qualify a useful measured spectrum first, followed by a regional spectral-signature map only if native geometry supports it.
proposals.evidence: The archive distinguishes 117,937 raw spectra from 111,226 calibrated Itokawa spectra. Other targets and calibration frames must not be mistaken for asteroid coverage.
proposals.work: Read original wavelength/calibration records, select target and epoch, preserve quality and uncertainty, and join observation geometry before assessing spatial coverage.
proposals.limit: Spectrum counts are not independent resolved surface cells. Do not infer mineral abundance or use AMICA texture detail to sharpen a NIRS footprint.
proposals.checks: Target filtering, native radiometric samples, wavelength order, uncertainty, footprint and current chart/map feasibility.

proposals.title: Ryugu: dated infrared temperature observations
proposals.current: Ryugu already has a modeled thermal-inertia view. Actual dated TIR observations are a different possible addition.
proposals.result: Qualify a compact, useful temperature observing set that preserves local solar time and measured footprint.
proposals.evidence: The Hayabusa2 TIR bundle contains operational instrument products; the inventory alone does not establish a ready global temperature map.
proposals.work: Prefer calibrated or derived products, resolve radiance versus brightness temperature, join camera geometry and uncertainty, and prepare a bounded set offline.
proposals.limit: Thermal inertia and temperature have different units and meanings. No false simultaneous global mosaic from changing illumination.
proposals.checks: Source calibration, time/local time, independent temperatures, registration and a distinct result beyond the current thermal-inertia product.

proposals.title: Ryugu: MASCOT's local temperature measurements
proposals.current: Global thermal inertia does not represent the lander's local thermal time series.
proposals.result: Qualify a local temperature curve or measured thermal facts using existing chart content, with the landing-site context retained.
proposals.evidence: The archive contains MASCOT MARA radiometer observations and separate bus records that can support timing and state interpretation.
proposals.work: Read instrument calibration, channel responses, pointing and lander states; isolate the usable surface intervals and preserve uncertainty.
proposals.limit: Do not extrapolate a lander-sized measurement across Ryugu or confuse instrument temperature with surface temperature. No surface panorama UI.
proposals.checks: Native time/channel samples, state filtering, footprint/pointing, uncertainty and current chart compatibility.

proposals.title: Eros and Ryugu: measured magnetic constraints
proposals.current: The audit has not compared these instrument results with each body's existing magnetic-property facts.
proposals.result: Add or correct published magnetic limits or a bounded measurement curve where it adds useful scientific content.
proposals.evidence: NEAR MAG includes calibrated and derived results; MASCOT carries a separate fluxgate magnetometer archive.
proposals.work: Identify final science products, frame and background/spacecraft-field corrections; compare published limits and uncertainties to current facts.
proposals.limit: A measured field near an asteroid is not automatically intrinsic magnetization. An upper limit must not become zero or a fabricated global magnetic map.
proposals.checks: Original calibrated units, background treatment, statistical limit definition, epoch and independent published comparisons.

proposals.title: Moon and giant-planet systems: measured dust observations
proposals.current: These detector and infrared measurements were outside the original surface-map shortlist. They may support existing chart or factual content without changing rendering.
proposals.result: Qualify a small set of published dust-flux, particle-distribution or infrared-brightness measurements, with separate source decisions for each observing system.
proposals.evidence: CDA/HRD, Galileo DDS, LADEE LDEX, Ulysses and MSX measure different particle or line-of-sight quantities; their archives are independently listed in PDS4.
proposals.work: Start from calibrated or published derived products, retain detection efficiency, spacecraft position, viewing direction, time and uncertainty, and identify an existing content owner.
proposals.limit: No fabricated surface dust map, animated particles or three-dimensional density inferred directly from a detector count. A source without a faithful current-contract presentation remains an evidence-only result.
proposals.checks: Counts versus physical flux, calibration/selection effects, geometry, uncertainty and useful source-backed facts or charts.

proposals.title: Explain spectral signatures with measured laboratory references
proposals.current: The tool needs understandable explanations of mineral and ice signatures. A laboratory spectrum can support an existing chart but does not measure a planetary surface.
proposals.result: Add a small number of clearly labeled laboratory comparisons beside relevant measured spectra, only through an already supported chart contract.
proposals.evidence: The archive includes temperature-dependent water-ice spectra/optical constants, meteorite reflectance spectra and olivine absorption spectra across iron/magnesium compositions.
proposals.work: Choose a concrete existing scientific comparison, retain sample composition, temperature, grain/preparation method and units, and verify that normalization remains meaningful.
proposals.limit: No claim that a laboratory sample uniquely identifies surface minerals or determines abundance. Ice transmission, optical constants and asteroid reflectance are not interchangeable curves.
proposals.checks: Native samples, units, sample conditions, normalization and a scientifically justified comparison with plain-language labels.

proposals.title: Pluto: observed atmospheric occultation profiles
proposals.current: Pluto has surface ice and height data. A stellar occultation samples atmospheric transmission rather than surface composition.
proposals.result: Qualify the 2007 simultaneous visible/infrared occultation curve or published atmospheric constraints through existing charts and facts.
proposals.evidence: The PDS4 package records the March 18 grazing occultation with continuous observations and timing metadata.
proposals.work: Retrieve calibrated light curves, geometry, time scale and uncertainties; retain the distinction between observations and any retrieved atmospheric profile.
proposals.limit: A grazing chord is not a global pressure map. Do not change atmospheric rendering or derive an unconstrained three-dimensional structure.
proposals.checks: Time alignment between bands, normalization, station geometry, uncertainty and published-model reproduction if a profile is retained.

proposals.title: Small bodies: calibrated MSX infrared observations
proposals.current: No row-level comparison of these measured infrared observations with existing comet and asteroid content has been completed.
proposals.result: Identify a bounded set of missing measured spectra, photometric points or supported image layers for existing objects.
proposals.evidence: The archive contains calibrated Spirit III images of eight comets, two transition objects and two near-Earth asteroids in six infrared bands.
proposals.work: Join original target IDs, source apertures, band responses, observation geometry and uncertainties; distinguish nucleus, coma and background contributions.
proposals.limit: Six bands do not imply six resolved surface maps. No invented comet shape or new dust renderer; unresolved measurements belong in charts or facts.
proposals.checks: Target matching, calibration, aperture/background treatment, epoch and distinct value over existing observations.

proposals.title: Small bodies: qualify historical map observations
proposals.current: Many represented bodies already have better spacecraft maps. The collection title alone does not establish missing data.
proposals.result: Identify individual historical map sheets or photographic observations that add a useful epoch, footprint or source interpretation to an existing package.
proposals.evidence: The Stooke archive contains 270 map sheets covering six asteroids, five satellites and three comets; the Thomas collection also includes image mosaics.
proposals.work: Inventory each sheet's underlying observations, projection and target ID, compare it with selected current maps, and keep a named acceptance or rejection for every proposed addition.
proposals.limit: No automatic new-body count, replacement geometry or reinterpretation of a cartographic reconstruction as a resolved photograph. Map-sheet counts are not unique observations.
proposals.checks: Original image lineage, coordinate support, current-source overlap, source reuse terms and measurable incremental value.

proposals.title: Moon: Clementine spectral bands and calibration comparison
proposals.current: The Moon already has derived mineral signatures and Kaguya products. A Clementine measured-band set is a distinct instrument source, but its calibration variants are not independent observations.
proposals.result: Qualify a compact Clementine UVVIS/NIR band group if it adds useful wavelength or historical coverage beyond the selected products.
proposals.evidence: The USGS audit identifies five-band warped UVVIS and two NIR calibration releases. Their native scale and cross-instrument consistency need qualification.
proposals.work: Compare the two NIR calibration methods, preserve per-band validity and wavelength, and check the warped grid against Kaguya on common footprints.
proposals.limit: No mineral abundance inferred from a ratio press image, duplicated standard/empirical rows or assumption that all bands are quantitatively comparable.
proposals.checks: Native scaling and masks, published calibration limits, wavelength order, numeric samples and measured benefit over existing datasets.

proposals.title: Moon: qualify the published polar ice-favorability model
proposals.current: Existing lunar thermal, rock and illumination inputs do not themselves establish this combined favorability score.
proposals.result: Determine whether the published north/south polar index adds an understandable, reproducible model interpretation through an existing data view.
proposals.evidence: The USGS catalogue exposes separate polar index products. This is a model lead, not a direct ice detection or water-abundance observation.
proposals.work: Read the index definition, input epochs, weighting and missing-data treatment; retrieve native values and compare with selected underlying measurements.
proposals.limit: Label the quantity as modeled favorability. Do not equate a high score with confirmed ice, probability of ice unless the model defines that, or current exploration guidance.
proposals.checks: Published formula, native value range, polar registration, uncertainty/limitations and incremental educational value beyond the measured inputs.

proposals.title: Venus: published regional geological units
proposals.current: Venus radar and numeric surface measurements do not supply these interpreted regional geological boundaries.
proposals.result: Qualify original categorical mapping for the Snegurochka Planitia and Metis Mons quadrangles using the existing geological-map contract.
proposals.evidence: The USGS audit found the two regional map records and TIFF evidence; original unit and coordinate support still need inspection.
proposals.work: Prefer the original GIS or categorical map over a flattened illustrated plate; preserve unit codes, mapped scale, projection and source interpretation.
proposals.limit: No claim of complete global coverage or absolute terrain ages from relative units. Keep this a regional option, reflecting the user's preference for substantial useful coverage.
proposals.checks: Original GIS availability, category/legend agreement, native boundaries, projection and useful footprint at current zoom.

proposals.title: Moon: qualify historical and illumination-specific photographs
proposals.current: Modern global lunar photography already exists. These sources would add a qualified historical or illumination comparison rather than automatically improve spatial detail.
proposals.result: Retain one genuinely distinct source-qualified observing set if its date or lighting adds scientific value within existing controls.
proposals.evidence: The USGS audit includes Lunar Orbiter imagery, a hybrid mosaic and Kaguya morning/evening products. The hybrid combines instruments rather than representing a single exposure.
proposals.work: Read source-image lineage, illumination and projection; cross-match current inputs and quantify registration and footprint before choosing a set.
proposals.limit: Do not turn lighting differences into surface-change claims or label a multi-epoch hybrid as one historical date. No duplicate dataset for a cosmetic alternate basemap.
proposals.checks: Original epochs and observing geometry, source overlap, control residuals, validity and an explicit reason the addition is useful.

proposals.title: Asteroids: measured radar Doppler spectra
proposals.current: Radar shape models and optical reflectance spectra do not preserve the measured radar echo profiles in this archive.
proposals.result: Qualify selected original Doppler profiles for existing bodies through the current chart or factual-content contract.
proposals.evidence: The PDS4 bundle identifies comma-separated Arecibo Doppler spectra associated with Virkki et al. (2022). These are whole-target echo measurements, not surface photographs.
proposals.work: Join target and observation IDs, record transmit frequency, polarization, Doppler convention, normalization and noise, and compare current radar-property facts before adding a representative profile.
proposals.limit: Do not turn echo frequency into a surface longitude or infer material abundance from radar brightness. A shape inversion is a separate model, outside this proposal.
proposals.checks: Native numeric samples, Doppler units/sign, polarization channels, calibration/noise and a faithful existing-chart presentation.
